entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Secure Savin Keep, free its bound defenders, and recover the first strong historical evidence of Tyren.
Bellweather needs Savin Keep to secure the harbor approach, but the ruined keep is still defended by undead bound to old orders.
Holding Savin Keep gives the city a strategic foothold and yields historical evidence naming Tyren as a force connected to Bellweather’s earlier fall.
{@b Leads onward.} The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Solve/bypass the undead defenses, break the binding, hold the keep during the counterattack.
{@b Player agency.} Research before departure, parley with bound spirits, use passwords, or force a military solution.
{@b Fail forward.} Passwords and historical clues have redundant sources. Missing one changes difficulty, not solvability.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Keep the {@item Potion of Heroism}, the hidden historical records, and either a {@item +1 Warhammer} or {@item +1 Shield}. Convert the remaining stockpile of permanent magic weapons into 500 gp of salvage and ceremonial equipment for the new garrison.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Keep the undead premise. Use {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}, {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}, {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters}, and one {@creature Wight|XMM} as patrol leadership. Keep {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} where appropriate. Replace the mass counterattack with a tactical force such as a {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblins}, 2 {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, and 2 {@b Worgs}, adjusting counts to the party's current strength.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Savin Keep stands on an island guarding Bellweather's harbor approach. The Council waits until nearby waters and landing points are reasonably secure before authorizing the mission. The objective is not to exterminate everything on the island; it is to make the keep safe enough for a permanent garrison and recover whatever records survived the fall.

entries.name: Approach and Passwords
entries: Three fragments—{@b Lux}, {@b Shestnik}, and {@b Samosud}—appear on old notes and plaques around the keep. Characters can learn that they were challenge-and-response phrases used by the final defenders. Discovering any two makes the third easier to infer from Ferren Marten's records. The passwords let the party bypass some undead guardians, but they are not required to complete the chapter.

entries.name: 1. Outside the Gate
entries: A weathered skeleton lies among reeds and stones. Its equipment is ruined, but a corroded medallion and partial note preserve two password fragments. A careful search also reveals tracks from a recent hostile reconnaissance team.

entries.name: 2. Gate and Courtyard
entries: The wooden gate is barely functional. Inside, the courtyard is patrolled by a small group of {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} bound to the keep's final defense. Use one encounter appropriate to the party's level; the guardians ignore anyone who gives the correct password. Once combat begins, they fight until destroyed or the party withdraws beyond the gate.

entries.name: 3. Stable
entries: A collapsed stable contains an obvious patch of chemically damaged timber. Disturbing the rafters releases a {@creature Gray Ooze|XMM} or other corrosive creature or hazard appropriate to the party. The danger is telegraphed by dissolved nails and pitted stone.

entries.name: 4. Granary
entries: Pale fungus grows across old grain bins. A character proficient with Nature, Medicine, or an herbalism kit can identify a harmless restorative strain. Harvesting it yields one use that grants advantage on the next saving throw against the Frightened condition made before the next Long Rest.

entries.name: 5. Smithy
entries: The smithy is home to several territorial {@b Giant Frogs} or another small coastal predator. Behind the hearth lies a well-preserved weapon from the old garrison. Replace the original generic +1 weapon with one uncommon martial item appropriate to the party or with a named heirloom that can be returned to Bellweather for reputation.

entries.name: 6. Barracks
entries: The ruined barracks hold echoes of the final defenders. These manifestations do not attack. If greeted respectfully or with a password, they point out a hidden diary describing the unnatural coordination of the armies that destroyed Bellweather. This is an automatic clue to Tyren's historical influence.

entries.name: 7. Kitchen
entries: An {@creature Ochre Jelly|XMM} has spread through the ruined kitchen. A sour mineral odor, warped metal, and partially dissolved wood warn attentive characters. Roll Initiative normally if the party enters carelessly. The room contains salvage and one consumable reward after the creature is dealt with.

entries.name: 8. Entrance Hall — Counterattack
entries: When the party reaches the watchtower interior, a Tyren-aligned strike team lands on the island to prevent reclamation. Use a compact force such as one {@creature Veteran|XMM} commander, two {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, and four {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} or equivalent creatures. Their objective is to seize the gate and burn the surviving records, not to fight to the last creature. If the commander falls or half the force is defeated, the survivors withdraw toward their boats.
The undead guardians oppose the strike team as readily as they oppose the characters. Clever parties can exploit that conflict.

entries.name: 9. Armory
entries: Most racks are empty. An illusory wall conceals a surviving cache. Award one uncommon permanent item, one consumable, and mundane salvage rather than several stacking +1 items.

entries.name: 10. Officer's Quarters
entries: A nearly transparent predator—use an appropriate ooze, mimic-like creature, or {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM} only if the party's tier supports it—has made this room its hunting ground. Scratches and dragged dust provide warning. A parchment here contains the final password fragment.

entries.name: 11. Old Chapel
entries: The spirit of {@b Ferren Marten}, last chaplain of Savin Keep, appears near the altar. He is not inherently hostile. If the party identifies themselves as Bellweather's reclaimers and treats the dead with respect, Ferren explains that Bellweather fell because powerful leaders were unnaturally unified by a force associated with a radiant pool. He names {@b Tyren}, {@b Edra}, and {@b Toran}, and points the party toward records once kept at Marren Library.

Ferren then releases the remaining defender-spirits from their duty. If attacked, use a {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} chassis appropriate to the party, but the scene is intended as revelation rather than combat.

entries.name: Securing Savin Keep
entries: The mission succeeds when the party has broken the binding on the defenders, prevented the counterattack from destroying the site, and made the approach safe enough for a Council garrison. On return, shipping begins expanding almost immediately.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Crossing
entries: The party leads the first landing while a small Bellweather guard detachment waits offshore for a signal.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stealth or bad weather can conceal the boat. Bright light or loud magic alerts the gate.
Old signal bells begin ringing without visible hands as the party approaches.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The keep appears abandoned but reacts to intruders according to ancient routines.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: An undetected landing lets the party inspect the gate before combat.

entries.name: Scene 2: Gate and Courtyard
entries: Undead defenders continue commands issued during Bellweather’s last fall.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They hold assigned posts and do not pursue far beyond them.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 6 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}, 2 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A guardroom tablet says “hold until relieved by lawful command,” implying the binding can be ended.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Destroying every undead works, but learning the release phrase reduces later resistance.

entries.name: Scene 3: Barracks and Shrine
entries: A ruined shrine preserves the oath formula used by the last commander.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters who search the shrine find the release phrase and learn that speaking it at the command stone can end the old watch.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The oath names the last commander and confirms the undead were defenders, not invaders.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This discovery reframes the keep as a tragedy rather than a monster nest.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Stone
entries: The binding focus is defended by the last commander’s wight.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking the release phrase causes ordinary skeletons to stop fighting immediately.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Wight|XMM}, 4 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A sealed report names Tyren as a possessing force linked to disturbances around the Radiant Well generations ago.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This is the first historical evidence that the present “Boss” may be connected to an older threat.

entries.name: Scene 5: Counterattack
entries: Living Tyren-aligned troops attack before Bellweather can occupy the keep.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party must hold either the dock or gate for 5 rounds. At the end of round 5, Bellweather reinforcements arrive.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 4 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}, 2 {@creature Worg|XMM|Worgs}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Holding the keep secures the harbor route and turns the site into a Bellweather garrison.

entries.name: Scene 6: Records of Ownership
entries: Old inventories recovered from the keep identify surviving archives tied to the Cardon family’s Weavehouse.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests access to the records and proposes reclaiming the Weavehouse next.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The records are genuine and establish a plausible Cardon claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 7 if using milestones.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 8
entries: The Council approves an expedition to Cardon Weavehouse, where property, occupants, and old records collide.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Potion of Heroism, +1 Shield (default; swap to +1 Warhammer if party needs weapon), 500 gp salvage, historical records.

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Reclaim the Cardon Weavehouse and force the party to confront the difference between public risk and private inheritance.
Perrin Cardon asks the Council to reclaim his family’s old Weavehouse, presenting the mission as both civic recovery and restoration of lawful ownership.
Whatever the decision, Perrin recovers enough wealth and documentation to become a much more influential figure in Bellweather.
{@b Leads onward.} The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Secure the building, identify the real ownership/treasure question, survive rival claims.
{@b Player agency.} Honor Cardon’s claim, challenge it, negotiate public use, or bargain for concessions.
{@b Fail forward.} The Cardon history is discoverable through multiple records and witnesses.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Most recovered wealth belongs to the property itself or the Cardon claim. Let the party recover {@b 500–750 gp} in immediate valuables and one uncommon permanent item at most. The larger economic reward is Cardon's restored fortune and rising influence.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Favor current urban predators and occupiers: {@creature Ettercap|XMM} + {@b Giant Spiders}, {@b Wererats}, {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears}, {@b Veterans}, or another group that makes sense for the current district. Preserve the family's hidden-wealth story rather than any specific specific creature count.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Council authorizes reclamation of the old Cardon property after the surrounding route is reasonably secure. Perrin publicly frames the mission as civic recovery, but privately wants proof of ownership and the family cache returned to him.

Before departure, Perrin offers {@b Taren Vale}, an aging household retainer represented by a {@creature Scout|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} as appropriate. Taren remembers the old layout imperfectly and can sketch the broad plan. His private instruction is to identify Cardon heirlooms and report what the party finds. He does not steal from the characters or force the outcome.

If the party recovers disputed property, Perrin first attempts a legal claim through the Council. The characters can accept compensation, challenge the claim with records, negotiate public use, or demand an independent hearing. The Council is institutionally inclined to protect documented ownership, but it is not predetermined to side with Perrin. Reputation, evidence, and witnesses matter.

entries.name: Occupying Warband
entries: A Tyren-aligned mixed warband currently controls the Weavehouse. Most members are gnolls, but species is not the faction's moral identity. The complex also contains dependents, injured people, coerced workers, and younger noncombatants. Those people flee, hide, or surrender if given a safe route.
The warband uses an alarm drum. Once raised, patrols consolidate around the courtyard, gates, and chief's hall rather than spawning endless reinforcements.

entries.name: 1. Outer Gates and Courtyard
entries: The old Cardon crest is still visible beneath the warband's angular red mark. During the day, one patrol watches the courtyard; at night, more off-duty members gather here around fires. The party can infiltrate over a wall, bluff at a gate, enter through collapsed structures, or trigger a direct fight.

entries.name: 2. Collapsed Wing
entries: Burned-out structures contain refuse, unstable flooring, and a corrosive ooze. The area also provides a concealed route around the main courtyard for characters willing to crawl through debris.

entries.name: 3. Watchpost
entries: A distracted three-person patrol watches one approach. Their duty roster contains Tyren's seal and references tribute demanded from multiple independent factions—useful evidence that the Boss is coordinating more than one group.

entries.name: 4–5. Former Servants' Quarters
entries: These rooms house junior guards and people low in the warband hierarchy. They are the easiest occupants to convince to stand down, especially if the party promises safe passage. One knows where prisoners and noncombatants are being kept.

entries.name: 6. Main Hall
entries: The warband leader uses this former reception hall as a command post. Use a gnoll leader if one fits the party's level; otherwise use a {@creature Gladiator|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM} with gnoll appearance and a small escort. The leader's goal is to preserve control of the site and escape with Tyren's correspondence if defeat becomes likely.

entries.name: 7–9. Living Quarters
entries: These rooms contain dependents, wounded members, and off-duty retainers. Treat them as a social and moral complication, not an encounter quota. If the party indiscriminately attacks noncombatants, Neighborhoods & Workers and Independent Factions reputation suffer.

entries.name: 10. Garden
entries: The old kitchen garden has gone wild. A hidden cistern provides a quiet route between buildings and can serve as a defensible short-rest location once secured.

entries.name: 11. Cardon Bedroom and Cache
entries: The family cache is concealed behind old plaster. A ten-minute search finds it automatically; a successful DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) check finds it immediately. The art objects are historically and legally significant, not merely loot. Their total market value is substantial, but the chapter's {@b Treasure Override} determines what portable wealth the party actually receives.
Finding the cache creates the chapter's central choice: return it to Perrin, place it in Council custody, use Marren Library records to challenge ownership, or negotiate a public settlement.

entries.name: 12. Shrine and Correspondence
entries: A spiritual leader represented by a {@creature Priest|XMM} or {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM} keeps Tyren's letters and tribute demands. The correspondence makes clear that the warband is being rewarded for obedience and threatened for independence. This is another automatic clue to the Boss's methods.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The site is reclaimed when the command structure is broken, civilians and dependents are no longer trapped inside, and the Council can occupy the property without immediate counterattack. What happens to the property itself is a political question, not a dungeon reward.

entries.name: Scene 1: Perrin’s Claim
entries: Perrin presents deeds showing that his family owned the Weavehouse before Bellweather fell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: He asks the party to secure the property and preserve surviving records. He does not ask them to harm current occupants.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin genuinely believes restored ownership will attract investment and stabilize Bellweather.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Workers warn that several families and a small armed band now use the complex.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party can seek relocation guarantees before entering.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Courtyard Occupants
entries: Civilian squatters live under the protection of a warband that charges them for food and safety.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Speaking with civilians first identifies which structures contain fighters and which contain families.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Mara Pell speaks for the families and wants time plus guaranteed relocation. Korrin Vale leads the armed group and wants the stored goods.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Residents know the records vault has remained sealed.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Treating civilians fairly earns durable neighborhood support.

entries.name: Scene 3: Armed Wing
entries: Korrin’s fighters hold the warehouse and counting room.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Korrin surrenders if isolated and reduced below half hit points. Civilians do not fight unless attacked.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Korrin uses {@creature Veteran|XMM}.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated surrender prevents unnecessary civilian displacement.

entries.name: Scene 4: Records Vault
entries: The sealed vault contains deeds, payrolls, debt books, and customer inventories.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Separate the documents into Cardon property, worker property, customer consignments, and public historical records.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The building belongs to the Cardon family, but not everything inside does. Correspondence mentions scholars at Marren Library studying “radiant disturbances” before the fall.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party’s handling of the records establishes a precedent others later cite.

entries.name: Scene 5: The Settlement
entries: Perrin, residents, workers’ descendants, and Council clerks make competing claims after the danger is gone.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can advocate for strict deed ownership, compensation and relocation, shared recovery, or another arrangement.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin accepts a lawful compromise in public even if it limits his gain; he remembers who opposed him.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Perrin gains enough wealth and standing to become a major Council voice. Marren Library becomes the obvious next historical target.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 9
entries: The Weavehouse correspondence points toward Marren Library, where pre-fall scholars investigated the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} 500–750 gp immediately portable value, one uncommon item (default {@b Sending Stones} found in old office), major property assets go into legal process.

entries: {@b Recommended level:} 8–9

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Recover Bellweather’s documentary memory and reveal Tyren as a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
Bellweather gains access to Marren Library, one of the best surviving collections of pre-fall records.
By the end of the chapter, the party should understand that Tyren is not merely a warlord but a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.
{@b Leads onward.} With valuable districts reopening, old families and investors begin pressing claims in the Mansion District.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Preserve records, identify Radiant Well references, choose who receives copies.
{@b Player agency.} Work for Cardon, work for the Council, copy records independently, or involve scholars/temples.
{@b Fail forward.} Core Pool/Radiant Well clues are guaranteed; checks determine how complete and private the discovery is.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override Knowledge is the reward. Give the party 2–4 useful spell scrolls appropriate to their level, one uncommon or rare utility item, and valuable manuscripts worth {@b 500 gp} if sold—or much more as leverage with scholars and the Council.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use constructs, undead scholars, and aberrant scavengers where the source calls for generic guardians: {@creature Animated Armor|XMM}, {@b Flying Sword}, {@creature Specter|XMM}, {@creature Ghoul|XMM}, {@creature Mimic|XMM}, {@b Gibbering Mouther}, or {@b Nothic}. Keep intelligent encounters conversational when possible.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Marren Library is valuable because it contains the documentary memory Bellweather lost when the city fell. Perrin wants specific records concerning old property, the Radiant Well, and the Cardon family's claims. The Council publicly describes the mission as preservation.

entries.name: Entering the Library
entries: The building is damaged but recognizable. Collapsed walls create multiple entrances. The party's challenge is less about clearing every room than about finding the right collections while protecting fragile records from hazards and opportunists.

entries.name: 1. Garden Court
entries: The contemplation garden has become a marshy overgrowth. Patches of {@b Green Slime} or another environmental hazard cling to shaded stones. Their presence is visible through bleached vegetation and pitted masonry; they do not gain special surprise bonuses.

entries.name: 2. Stacks and Subject Collections
entries: The library is divided into rhetoric, philosophy, mathematics, history, and practical records. Searching a relevant collection for one hour automatically yields its essential campaign clue; a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check reduces the time and uncovers an additional useful detail.

{@b Philosophy.} A surviving treatise on sacred springs warns that immersion can allow an external spirit to enter a willing or weakened host. Another text names {@b Tyren the Flamed One} among lesser extraplanar powers once associated with Bane.

{@b History.} An old atlas shows Bellweather and northern routes. A military chronicle describes Tyren leading armies while surrounded by supernatural flame, then surviving bodily destruction by moving between hosts before being imprisoned in radiant water. The account is incomplete but establishes that Tyren is a possessing intelligence rather than a single mortal warlord.

entries.name: 3. Master Librarian's Chamber
entries: The spirit of the last master librarian protects the collection from looters. Treat this as a social scene first. Characters who explain that they intend to preserve or copy the books can earn cooperation. If they attempt wholesale theft or destruction, use a {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} appropriate to the party.

entries.name: 4–6. Reading Rooms and Entrance Hall
entries: These areas contain rotted furniture, faded murals, and scattered fragments. They are useful for quiet exploration and for foreshadowing the institution Bellweather once was rather than for mandatory combat.

entries.name: 7. Scribes' Hall — Evan Rell
entries: Huddled behind a desk is {@b Evan Rell}, an exhausted survivor who has spent days hiding from patrols and whatever he witnessed near Varen Keep.

Evan is frightened, sleep-deprived, and initially defensive, but not irrational or automatically violent. Food, water, a calm approach, or magic that eases fear lets him share fragments: {@b “A figure wrapped in fire,” “something on the hill giving orders through other people,”} and {@b “the castle isn't the real danger—the thing using it is.”} These clues reinforce Tyren without requiring a check.
Evan wants an escort back to safety. Once in Bellweather, healers can treat his injuries and trauma over time. His recovery does not require memory erasure or magical personality alteration.

entries.name: 8–11. Workrooms and Carrels
entries: Most supplies are ruined, but careful salvage can recover a modest amount of gold leaf, inks, vellum, and tools. Use these as crafting materials or civic salvage rather than a large cash payout.

entries.name: 12. Damaged Stacks
entries: A {@creature Basilisk|XMM} or another appropriate ruin predator has nested among collapsed shelves. Its presence is foreshadowed by stone vermin, claw marks, and damaged masonry. Defeating or bypassing it protects a surviving map case and one curated consumable magic item.

entries.name: 13. Storeroom
entries: A small group of displaced scavengers is hiding here. They surrender or negotiate if treated as people rather than targets. They know which streets around the library are currently patrolled and can point the party toward a safe exit.

entries.name: The Historical Refrain
entries: Among pre-fall Council records is the circular quoted earlier in this chapter: {@b “There is no cause for alarm.”} It was issued while reports of coordinated hostile movement were already accumulating. This is the adventure's clearest historical echo of the title.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The party succeeds by securing the most important records and determining how they will be held. Giving everything to Perrin strengthens him. Putting the archive under Council or independent stewardship creates different political consequences. The essential Tyren clues are preserved regardless.

entries.name: Scene 1: Reaching the Library
entries: The library is structurally damaged and occupied by scavengers and magical hazards. The party’s objective is preservation as much as exploration.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A smoke plume from one wing means some records are already in danger. Characters can enter through the garden court, main hall, or a broken upper window.
Every hour spent without stabilizing the fire destroys one minor collection; this does not remove essential clues.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather scholars provide a list of three priority collections: civic annals, magical research, and property records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party must choose what to protect first, giving the expedition an immediate priority.

entries.name: Scene 2: Garden Court
entries: The court is overgrown and watched by creatures that have nested among the statues.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Moving carefully reveals signs of recent human passage leading to the stacks.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Gargoyle|XMM|Gargoyles} if the party disturbs the central monument. They defend the courtyard only.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A satchel dropped by scavengers contains copied page numbers from the magical research wing. Someone else is looking for the same records.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing or tracking the scavengers can reveal that they were paid anonymously.

entries.name: Scene 3: Stacks and Fire
entries: A collapsed lamp has started a spreading fire while frightened scavengers try to remove selected volumes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters can fight the fire, stop the scavengers, or split up. Three successful actions using water, magic, blankets, or DC 13 ability checks contain the fire.
The scavengers surrender if cornered; they were hired to recover specific research, not burn the building.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Their leader, Tessa Marr, was promised 200 gp by a masked intermediary and knows only a drop location.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} if negotiation fails.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The requested volumes concern the Radiant Well, possession, and “personality transference.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Saving the stacks earns scholar and public goodwill.

entries.name: Scene 4: Master Librarian’s Chamber
entries: The locked chamber contains the most coherent pre-fall account of Tyren.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A damaged ward triggers when the desk is forced. DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or dispel magic suppresses it; otherwise each creature in the room makes a DC 14 Wisdom save or is frightened until the end of its next turn.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The journal states that Tyren is an intelligence capable of occupying living hosts. The Radiant Well amplifies or facilitates the transfer. The author believed destroying a host would not necessarily destroy Tyren.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This changes the campaign’s central question from “Who is the Boss?” to “What is possessing the Boss’s agents or leader?”

entries.name: Scene 5: Property Archives
entries: The property wing contains deeds and debt records useful to Bellweather’s present-day disputes.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin requests originals relating to Cardon holdings. Council clerks want all civic records retained publicly. Scholars want conservation before distribution.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin is especially attentive here but remains within legal procedure.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Several records show how emergency powers during Bellweather’s fall transferred public assets into private hands.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Who controls these records affects later property disputes and Perrin’s political leverage.

entries.name: Scene 6: Return and Publication
entries: The party must decide who receives originals, copies, and public access.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: At minimum, the Tyren material can be copied before any ownership dispute is settled.
Brakkus urges making dangerous historical information available to more than one institution.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Essential revelation: Tyren is a possessing intelligence linked to the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 9 if using milestones. The next phase focuses on wealth and property returning to the city, beginning with the Mansions.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 10
entries: With valuable districts reopening, old families and investors begin pressing claims in the Mansion District.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} 3 useful spell scrolls of levels 2–4, one uncommon/rare utility item (default {@b Eyes of Minute Seeing}), manuscripts worth 500 gp if sold but more as leverage.

data.name: Chapter 10: The Mansions
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 8–9

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Resolve three property cases that establish how Bellweather treats inherited claims, current occupants, and public-use promises.
With major streets reopening, several families and investors ask the party to enter the old Mansion District and resolve competing claims.
Perrin uses the resulting legal climate to strengthen private ownership and his own political influence.
{@b Leads onward.} Reports from occupied territory describe a thriving illicit market in Paden Square where rival factions trade under a shared truce.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Recover heirlooms, expose false claims, protect residents, decide what is public/private salvage.
{@b Player agency.} Accept private commissions, demand public terms, mediate rival heirs, or prioritize public safety.
{@b Fail forward.} Documents needed to adjudicate a featured claim are always recoverable with investigation.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Table-Ready Use
entries: Treat the Mansion District as a flexible set of 1–2 session commissions from old families, investors, displaced descendants, and opportunists. Each commission should expose a different argument about ownership. Use the source map as a reusable neighborhood rather than clearing every building.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use the current party tier and the organized-town encounter guidance. Private employers may accompany the party, creating protection and social complications. Keep family claims and hidden vaults central.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Mansion District was once home to Bellweather's richest families. Decades of abandonment, occupation, looting, and fire have left most properties damaged, but old vaults, legal records, heirlooms, and sealed rooms make the district newly valuable as reclamation reaches the river.

The Council has no single military objective here. Instead, the party receives competing commissions from descendants, current residents, investors, neighborhood advocates, and civic officials. The point of the chapter is not to clear every mansion. Run {@b three featured property cases}, each presenting a different question about ownership.

entries.name: Featured Case A — The Vell House
entries: {@b Claim.} Mara Vell, a descendant with credible records, wants family portraits and a sealed deed box recovered.
{@b Complication.} Two families have been living in the service wing for six years and have repaired part of the property.
{@b Opposition.} 2 {@b Gargoyles} and 2 {@b Animated Armors} remain bound to the old house.
{@b Choice.} Recover the heirlooms without displacing the residents; negotiate a tenancy; or turn the entire claim over to a Council hearing.

entries.name: Featured Case B — The Doran Vault
entries: {@b Claim.} Two distant heirs present conflicting documents.
{@b Complication.} A professional recovery crew led by a {@creature Veteran|XMM} has already entered under a private contract.
{@b Opposition.} A {@creature Mimic|XMM}, unstable floors, and the rival crew if negotiations fail.

{@b Evidence.} The vault contains a notarized codicil showing that part of the estate was gifted to a public hospice before Bellweather fell. This evidence is found automatically if the vault is opened.

entries.name: Featured Case C — The Harroway Garden
entries: {@b Claim.} An investor wants the property cleared for redevelopment.
{@b Complication.} A small community of squatters has converted the surviving courtyard into homes and workshops.
{@b Opposition.} A territorial {@creature Shambling Mound|XMM} in the overgrown conservatory is the actual danger. The residents are not enemies.
{@b Choice.} Clear only the monster and leave the civic dispute to negotiation, support the investor's claim, or advocate for a new use agreement.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The chapter is complete after the party resolves three substantial property cases or otherwise establishes a precedent that changes how Bellweather handles reclaimed estates. Their choices determine which factions gain reputation and how later residents talk about the party.

entries.name: Structure of the Chapter
entries: Run the Mansion District as three separate cases. Each mixes physical danger with a property dispute. The party can resolve them in any order.

entries.name: Case A: The Vell House
entries: A legitimate heir, Sera Vell, asks the party to clear her family home, which is occupied by dangerous creatures and a caretaker family that has lived there for years.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Clear the unsafe upper floor, then determine what happens to the caretakers.
Sera has valid title and is not cruel; the caretakers have nowhere else to go.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Sera wants her home back but agrees to reasonable relocation terms. The caretaker, Old Ren, distrusts promises made by officials.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 2 {@creature Ettercap|XMM|Ettercaps} and 3 {@creature Giant Spider|XMM|Giant Spiders} in the sealed upper rooms.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The house records show the Vells paid city taxes even after evacuation, strengthening the legal claim.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A negotiated tenancy or relocation earns goodwill from both sides. Immediate eviction helps strict property advocates but harms residents.

entries.name: Case B: The Doran Vault
entries: A wealthy claimant named Joric Doran presents documents claiming a sealed townhouse and its vault.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The deed is convincing at first glance. Inside, the party encounters traps and an old household guardian.
A careful search reveals the claim papers are altered copies.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Joric is charming, impatient, and offers the party a private bonus to “avoid delays.”

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM} as the old vault guardian. It attacks anyone lacking the original family signet.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The true deed names a different family whose surviving descendants are poor laborers in Bellweather. DC 14 Intelligence (Investigation) spots inconsistencies in Joric’s papers even before the original is found.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Exposing the fraud embarrasses several officials who endorsed Joric. Accepting his claim gives Perrin ammunition to argue that private verification should replace public review.

entries.name: Case C: Harroway Garden
entries: A once-grand estate is now home to dozens of squatters and a productive community garden.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The danger comes from a buried cistern contaminated by an {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. Clearing it makes the property far more valuable.
Afterward, investors offer to buy the claim from a distant heir who has never visited Bellweather.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Community leader Nessa Harroway is not related to the old owners; she took the name from the district. She wants legal recognition for current residents.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Otyugh|XMM}. The fight takes place around narrow cistern walkways; falling into the sewage imposes the Poisoned condition until the creature takes a short rest and washes.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The old estate records contain no surviving direct heir, only a chain of speculative claims.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Supporting current occupants creates a precedent for use-based claims. Supporting investors creates a precedent favoring documented ownership and capital.

entries.name: District Resolution
entries: Once all three cases are resolved, the Council debates what precedents they establish.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Perrin argues for predictable ownership rules. Bishop Brann argues that reclamation should not create homelessness. Wern cares mainly that disputes do not destabilize security.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin cites the party’s own decisions selectively, whichever ones support his position.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: These legal precedents matter later when Perrin uses institutional authority against the characters.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 11
entries: Reports from occupied territory describe a thriving illicit market in Paden Square where rival factions trade under a shared truce.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Each case pays 250–500 gp or equivalent favor. Limit chapter to one rare item total, default {@b Ring of Protection} from a voluntarily surrendered heirloom claim only if party resolves the public-use dispute fairly; otherwise replace with 750 gp in art/coin.

data.name: Chapter 11: Paden Square
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 9–10

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/paden_square.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/paden_square.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Infiltrate or turn Paden Square, identify Tyren’s agents, and prove the Boss coordinates trade as well as military force.
Scouts learn that Paden Square has become a functioning market inside occupied territory and that representatives of several hostile factions trade there.
The recovered correspondence proves that Bellweather is facing an organized strategic enemy rather than unrelated gangs.
{@b Leads onward.} The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Control exits, protect civilians, seize command correspondence, or convince part of the force to defect.
{@b Player agency.} Direct assault, infiltration, staged trade, sabotage, or faction negotiation.
{@b Fail forward.} Command evidence is not lost because one courier escapes; another source remains.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: No Cause for Alarm Beat
entries: After the party brings back evidence that supposedly separate hostile groups are coordinating, an official Council statement describes the activity as {@b "localized resistance"} and says there is {@b "no cause for alarm within Reclaimed Bellweather."} The statement may be technically true—the walls are still holding—but it minimizes what the characters have actually learned.
If the party brings the notice to Ledger House, Brakkus can read the final sentence and reply, {@b "Well. That settles it, then."} He immediately starts checking the shutters and cellar stores.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Present the plaza as a functioning hostile market rather than a room-by-room extermination. Social infiltration, bargaining, disguise, and violence should all work.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Paden Square was once Bellweather's commercial heart and remains a trading nexus inside occupied territory. The Council learns that a supposedly powerful magic item will be auctioned there and that the Boss may send a representative.

entries.name: Entering the Square
entries: Paden Square is busy, commercially active, and occupied by people from many factions and species. The party can enter as merchants, hired guards, couriers, bidders, entertainers, laborers, or invited guests. Cover depends on credentials and behavior, not ancestry.

If the characters' cover is weak, use a group Charisma (Deception) check against DC 14. On a failure, security questions them, demands a sponsor, or escorts them away; combat is only one possible consequence.

entries.name: Security and Scale
entries: The square is too crowded and fortified for a sensible direct assault, but do not represent that with hundreds of combatants. A frontal attack triggers escalating security, civilian panic, blocked exits, and a clear need to withdraw. Use one immediate security encounter and then a chase or escape procedure.

entries.name: Scene 1: Mission and Cover
entries: Paden Square is an active market inside hostile territory. The objective is intelligence, not extermination.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can enter disguised as buyers, escort a cooperating merchant, sneak across rooftops, or stage a diversion.
Their goals are to identify who enforces the truce, learn what the “Boss” is purchasing, and seize correspondence if possible.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Bellweather knows representatives of several hostile factions attend the same market without fighting.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A violent entrance causes vendors and couriers to scatter, making intelligence harder to recover.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Market
entries: Run the square as a social environment before combat.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Merchants sell weapons, food, medicine, stolen civic goods, and information. Many are criminals, but some are ordinary people trading because official routes are closed.
The party can gather three pieces of intelligence through conversation, observation, bribery, or theft.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin, a goblin broker, is talkative and self-protective. Balden, a human enforcer, speaks for the market’s security committee. Neither is automatically hostile.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The “Boss” buys maps, old records, alchemical reagents, and captives with unusual magical exposure.
Couriers use the crossed-line mark and carry sealed packets toward Storen Gate.
The market truce is enforced by threats from a central command, not mutual trust.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Good social play can complete most objectives without combat.

entries.name: Scene 3: The Auction
entries: A private auction offers an old civic map, captured correspondence, and a magical research folio.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can bid, steal, expose a seller, or disrupt the auction.
If they win or seize the correspondence, it names Storen Gate as the primary logistics route.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Garin will quietly help the party if convinced Bellweather can keep the market open under safer rules later.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If combat starts, use 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}, and 2 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}. Civilians flee rather than fight.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The correspondence refers to the central commander only as “Boss,” but includes orders to move forces through Storen Gate and references “the host” in singular terms.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing documents is more important than defeating every enemy.

entries.name: Scene 4: Escape or Negotiated Exit
entries: Once the party’s purpose is exposed, exits begin to close.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: They can escape through alleys, bargain with Garin, create a crowd panic, or fight a delaying action.
Use a three-success chase if needed: Athletics, Acrobatics, Stealth, Deception, or clever magic.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A captured courier can confirm that orders ultimately come from Varen Keep.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the party is captured, market leaders prefer ransom or trade to execution; allies can create a second chance.

entries.name: Scene 5: Bellweather Learns the Scale
entries: The evidence proves the hostile network has logistics, markets, couriers, and strategic command.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Wern proposes taking Storen Gate to cut the supply route. Perrin supports the plan because it would open valuable interior districts.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 10 if using milestones.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 12
entries: The party is asked to lead the operation against Storen Gate before the enemy can reinforce it.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays 500 gp total for reliable intelligence and an additional 500 gp if the party secures the auctioned material for civic custody.

data.name: Chapter 12: Storen Gate
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 10–11

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/storen_gate.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/storen_gate.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Take Storen Gate as a strategic objective and open the safest land route into deeper ruins.
Storen Gate blocks the safest land route into the deeper ruins and allows Tyren-aligned forces to move troops without interference.
Capturing Storen Gate opens the city’s deeper districts and shifts the campaign from local reclamation to open strategic conflict.
{@b Leads onward.} With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Open/hold the gate, prevent a signal, defeat or turn the command element.
{@b Player agency.} Climb, infiltrate, bribe an insider, create a diversion, or conduct a frontal attack.
{@b Fail forward.} Failure to stop a signal adds reinforcements or pressure rather than ending the scenario.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Treat this as a military objective. Success is measured by controlling the alarm, gate mechanism, command post, and reinforcement timing rather than by defeating every defender.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: The Wall
entries: Characters approaching openly are warned away from the wall and directed to the gate. Characters climbing, flying, or sneaking across contend with watch rotations, cover, and magical observation. Resolve the approach with the normal 2024 stealth, perception, and spell rules rather than percentage detection.

entries.name: The Gate
entries: Merchant wagons still pass through under permit, which gives the party several options:

items: buy or borrow a legitimate wagon and paperwork;
forge a permit or impersonate a supply crew;
hide among cargo and make a group Dexterity (Stealth) check against the guards' passive Perception;
bribe a corrupt clerk;
create a distraction elsewhere on the wall;
attack directly.

entries: Failure does not mean instant combat. Guards question the party, demand inspection, separate one character for verification, or call an officer. Combat begins only if the situation escalates there.

entries.name: Capturing the Gate
entries: The gate can be secured by defeating the command group, convincing enough troops to stand down, or disabling the portcullis and signal system long enough for Bellweather's forces to arrive. Once the defenders' command collapses, rank-and-file troops may retreat or surrender.

entries.name: Scene 1: Planning the Assault
entries: Storen Gate is a military objective with four goals: silence the alarm, open the gate, seize the command post, and hold it.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can choose stealth, climbing, sabotage, infiltration with captured signals, or direct assault.
Bellweather troops wait out of sight until the gate opens or a signal is given.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Scouts identify the alarm tower, gate mechanism, barracks, and command post on the keyed map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Each objective completed before open combat reduces enemy reinforcements.

entries.name: Scene 2: The Wall
entries: Sentries control the outer wall and alarm bell.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: If the bell rings, add one additional group of defenders to the gate encounter after 2 rounds.
Cutting the bell rope, jamming the clapper, or silently removing the sentries prevents the reinforcement.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}, 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A signal chart shows Paden Square, Storen Gate, and Varen Keep on the same command network.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Silencing the alarm gives the party control over the pace of the assault.

entries.name: Scene 3: Gate Mechanism
entries: The mechanism room is defended because the enemy expects Bellweather to want the gate intact.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A character at the controls can open the gate with an action after the locking bar is removed. Removing it requires DC 15 Strength (Athletics) or two uninterrupted actions with tools.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM}, 4 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Opening the gate brings Bellweather troops into the battle at the start of the next round.

entries.name: Scene 4: Command Post
entries: The local commander tries to destroy orders and retreat toward the inner city.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Stop the commander, seize documents, or pursue if necessary.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Commander Vesk uses the {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM} stat block and values survival over martyrdom.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 1 {@creature Hobgoblin Captain|XMM}, 3 {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Orders refer to Tyren directly for the first time in contemporary documents and instruct commanders to “protect the host.”

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A living Vesk can confirm Tyren is not physically present at every command site.

entries.name: Scene 5: Hold the Gate
entries: The party must hold the command position until Bellweather forces secure both approaches.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Run 4 rounds of pressure rather than a mass battle. Each round presents one threat: archers, a breach, a retreating squad, or fire near the mechanism. Let the party choose where to intervene.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use small groups of {@creature Hobgoblin Warrior|XMM|Hobgoblin Warriors} or {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}; do not place dozens of creatures on the map.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Success opens the deeper city and marks the transition from reclamation to open war.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 13
entries: With the gate open, reports from Valen Cemetery become urgent: missing residents, opened graves, and organized undead movement.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Rewards.} The Council pays 1,000 gp total and provides one rare consumable or utility reward (default {@b Potion of Speed}). Captured military supplies become Council property.

data.name: Chapter 13: Valen Cemetery
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 11–12

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/valen_cemetery.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/valen_cemetery.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} End the escalating undead crisis, rescue abducted people, and reclaim Bellweather’s cemetery as a civic place for the dead.
Reports that began as disturbed graves have escalated into disappearances and organized undead attacks around Valen Cemetery.
Reclaiming the cemetery restores a civic place of mourning and removes one of the most visible signs that Bellweather’s recovery is failing.
{@b Leads onward.} Contaminated water and Hessa’s records lead directly to the laboratories on Maren Isle.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Protect the living, disrupt undead creation, identify and defeat the controlling threat.
{@b Player agency.} Research, holy support, stealth, daylight timing, or direct cleansing.
{@b Fail forward.} Lore needed to understand the source is given through graves, clergy, and survivors; checks add weaknesses/shortcuts.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Build the escalation from {@b Skeleton/Zombie} to {@b Ghoul/Ghast}, {@creature Wight|XMM}, {@creature Wraith|XMM}, {@creature Specter|XMM}, and finally the vampire or vampire-spellcaster equivalent appropriate to the party's level. Undead should arrive in distinct scenes rather than one giant attrition swarm.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Valen Cemetery has been deteriorating in the background for several chapters. Reports should escalate from disturbed graves, to wandering dead, to disappearances, to organized undead activity. Do not double monster counts by calendar math. Instead, advance the {@b Cemetery Threat} one step whenever the party completes a major chapter while ignoring the problem.

entries.name: Cemetery Threat

items: {@b Restless:} isolated {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} appear near the outer wall.
{@b Predatory:} {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls} and {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters} begin hunting after dark.
{@b Organized:} {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights} direct lesser undead and abduct victims.
{@b Crisis:} the controlling vampire or equivalent undead spellcaster begins sending forces beyond the cemetery.

entries: When the party finally acts, use the current threat step to add one complication, not to multiply every encounter.

entries.name: Entering Valen Cemetery
entries: The iron gates have burst outward. Withered vegetation, overturned stones, and several mausoleums divide the cemetery into distinct zones. Supernatural clouds dim the light once the party crosses the boundary, but ordinary and magical light function normally unless a specific creature says otherwise.

entries.name: Zone A — The Poor Graves
entries: The outer graves contain newly animated {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons} and signs that bodies have been removed from older plots. A large crypt houses the first control focus: a bound {@creature Specter|XMM} or {@creature Wraith|XMM} maintaining the animation. Breaking its funerary sigil, laying the spirit to rest, or defeating it stops new skeletons from rising.

entries.name: Zone B — The Marble Tower
entries: A ruined white tower contains {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies} and one stronger guardian such as a {@creature Wight|XMM}. The encounter objective is to reach the upper chamber and destroy a necromantic vessel before the dead overwhelm the stair. The vessel can be smashed, consecrated, or disabled with appropriate magic.

entries.name: Zone C — The Old Crypts
entries: This quarter is hunted by {@creature Ghoul|XMM|Ghouls}, {@b Ghasts}, and one {@creature Wight|XMM} commander. Prisoners taken from Bellweather are being held here for later transformation. Rescuing them is more important than clearing every crypt.

A sealed defender's tomb contains a curated cache: one rare defensive item, one uncommon weapon or shield suited to the party, and a {@item Ring of Fire Resistance} if it fits the adventure's treasure budget.

entries.name: Zone D — Memorial Court
entries: Statues and family vaults create a maze of cover. Several spirits here are not hostile; they can explain that the undead outbreaks are being directed from deeper in the cemetery. Respectful characters can receive the location of a hidden route into the inner mausoleum.

entries.name: Zone E — The Broken Chapel
entries: The chapel has been desecrated and converted into a staging point. Use a mixed encounter of {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights}, {@creature Specter|XMM|Specters}, and lesser undead appropriate to the party. Restoring the altar weakens the inner controller by removing one environmental effect from the finale.

entries.name: Zone F — Ossuary
entries: A collapsed ossuary is filled with unstable bone piles and narrow passages. Run this as an exploration hazard with one undead ambush at most. Recoverable names and burial records help Bellweather identify victims afterward.

entries.name: Zone G — The Generating Crypt
entries: A second necromantic focus continually reanimates nearby corpses. Characters can destroy the focus, reverse its runes, or use divine magic to consecrate it. Success prevents reinforcements during the finale.

entries.name: Zone H — False Tomb
entries: The apparent resting place of the controlling undead is a decoy containing staged evidence. Careful inspection automatically reveals inconsistencies if the characters spend ten minutes comparing it with clues from Marren Library or local clergy. Do not require a single check to avoid the false conclusion.

entries.name: Zone I — Inner Mausoleum
entries: The real controller retreats here: use a {@creature Vampire|XMM}, {@creature Vampire Spawn|XMM} spellcaster, or another undead leader appropriate to the party's level. The creature's goal is survival and continued control, not a static slugfest. It uses secret passages, dominated servants, and surviving necromantic focuses to shape the fight.

entries.name: Zone J — Resting Chamber
entries: The true resting chamber contains evidence connecting the undead crisis to Tyren's broader network, but the vampire is not necessarily Tyren's servant by ideology; it may simply be exploiting the same instability. This keeps the world from collapsing into one conspiracy.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: The cemetery is reclaimed when the controller is destroyed or permanently driven out and the necromantic focuses are disabled. Bellweather then holds public funerals, reburies identified dead, and creates a memorial rather than treating the site as another cleared dungeon.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Missing
entries: Families report that grave tenders and mourners have disappeared over several nights.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Bishop Brann asks the party to recover the missing if possible and stop whoever is using the cemetery.
Witnesses describe undead moving in groups toward the oldest crypts instead of wandering randomly.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The pattern suggests deliberate command.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A rescued victim can later identify the necromancer’s servants.

entries.name: Scene 2: Poor Graves
entries: The newest graves have been disturbed first because they are easiest to reach.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Tracks lead from opened graves toward an old service tunnel.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 6 {@creature Zombie|XMM|Zombies}. They are being used as labor and do not pursue far if bypassed.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Several bodies were removed without being animated, suggesting someone needs corpses elsewhere.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Re-consecrating or reburying the disturbed graves improves public trust.

entries.name: Scene 3: Marble Tower
entries: An old funerary tower serves as a lookout and holding point for captives.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Two missing grave tenders are alive inside. A signal lantern in the upper room can warn the crypts.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: 2 {@creature Wight|XMM|Wights}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: A list identifies bodies with unusual magical exposure—survivors of old Radiant Well incidents are specifically marked.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Preventing the signal gives advantage on the party’s first initiative check in the crypts.

entries.name: Scene 4: Old Crypts
entries: The controlling necromancer is using Tyren’s orders to identify corpses that might serve as suitable hosts or test subjects.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The ritual chamber includes a command focus. Destroying or disabling it causes lesser undead in the crypts to stop coordinating.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Necromancer Hessa Vale is ambitious and terrified of Tyren. She bargains with information if defeat is clear.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Mage|XMM} reskinned as a necromancer, 1 {@creature Wight|XMM}, and 4 {@creature Skeleton|XMM|Skeletons}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Hessa’s orders connect the cemetery work to magical experiments on Maren Isle. The phrase “viable host” appears repeatedly.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If Hessa escapes, her abandoned records still point to Maren Isle.

entries.name: Scene 5: Restoring the Cemetery
entries: The cemetery is a civic place of grief as much as a battlefield.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Let the party decide how much of the disturbing truth to tell families. Bishop Brann favors honesty without unnecessary detail.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Advance to level 12 if using milestones. Maren Isle becomes the next urgent lead because the Storen River is beginning to sicken people.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 14
entries: Contaminated water and Hessa’s records lead directly to the laboratories on Maren Isle.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} One rare defensive item (default {@b Cloak of Protection}), one uncommon weapon/shield, Ring of Fire Resistance, 600 gp funerary valuables that should be returned or handled respectfully.

data.name: Chapter 14: Maren Isle
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 12–13
