entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Stop the Storen River contamination, rescue experimental captives, and gain independent evidence about Radiant Well phenomena.
The Storen River becomes contaminated, sickening residents and threatening trade. Evidence points to experiments on Maren Isle.
Stopping the contamination restores the river route and gives the party crucial information for confronting Tyren later.
{@b Leads onward.} The research shows that Tyren is consolidating power beyond Bellweather as well as within it. The city needs allies and safe routes before a final confrontation.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Reach the source, disable or redirect magical systems, survive defenders.
{@b Player agency.} Seek expert advice, approach by water/air, negotiate with inhabitants, or force entry.
{@b Fail forward.} The contamination’s mechanism can be understood through multiple environmental clues.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Table-Ready Purpose
entries: This is a high-magic expedition. Favor {@b Elementals}, {@b Invisible Stalkers}, {@b Gargoyles}, {@b Helmed Horrors}, and mage-type NPCs. The island should reveal who or what poisoned the river and provide a major step toward reaching the Boss.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use spellcaster stat blocks such as {@creature Mage|XMM}, {@creature Archmage|XMM} (only when level-appropriate), {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}, and magical guardians such as {@creature Gargoyle|XMM}, {@creature Helmed Horror|XMM}, {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}, or elementals. Keep the pyramid/island exploration structure.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: The Storen River is being poisoned at its source by {@b Yaren}, an arcane experimenter operating from a pyramid on Maren Isle. The Council wants the contamination stopped because it blocks trade, sickens nearby districts, and prevents safe access toward Varen Keep.

entries.name: Following the River
entries: Residents, boat crews, healers, and regional travelers all provide overlapping information: the water is cleaner upstream until it reaches the island, the contamination resists ordinary purification, and strange lights are sometimes visible above the pyramid. These facts are automatic once the party asks around; checks reveal shortcuts, safe landing points, or details about Yaren's supply network.

entries.name: Reaching Maren Isle
entries: The southern water is saturated with alchemical waste. A creature that enters or drinks it makes a DC 15 Constitution saving throw, taking {@b 4d6 Poison damage} and gaining the {@b Poisoned} condition for 1 hour on a failure, or half damage with no condition on a success. Repeated exposure in the same hour increases the DC by 2.
Altered aquatic predators live near the discharge. Foreshadow them with wakes, dead fish, and movement under the surface rather than rolling random attacks every turn.
The pyramid has no obvious doors. Worn paths reveal concealed entrances on the north and south faces.

entries.name: Lower Level — The Maze
entries: Yaren uses the lower level to contain captives and failed recruits. The maze should feel tense without becoming a random-combat grinder.

{@b Prisoners.} A handful of survivors from different communities are trapped here. Hunger and fear make them cautious, not automatically hostile. Patient characters can gain information, temporary allies, and testimony against Yaren.

{@b The Keeper.} An elderly {@creature Priest|XMM} has survived by creating food and water and tending the others. He has been slowly weakening one exterior wall and can show the party a potential emergency exit.
{@b Second Maze.} Hardier prisoners and one or two dangerous altered creatures occupy this section. Use no more than one meaningful combat unless the party deliberately escalates.

{@b The Dead Writer.} A corpse hides a journal containing a rough map, a marked teleporter, and incomplete notes about Yaren's experiments. This is an automatic clue to the pyramid's internal movement system.

entries.name: Middle Level — Laboratories
entries: {@b Reedscale Cell.} Five Reedscale prisoners initially distrust anyone entering from Yaren's complex. Visible efforts to free captives, remove shackles, or share information establish good faith without a Persuasion check.
{@b Surgery.} Restraints, alchemical instruments, and recent blood make the purpose of the room clear. Keep descriptions within the table's agreed body-horror limits.

{@b Recovery Ward.} Several altered captives are in pain and frightened. They are victims, not monsters by default. Use a creature stat block only if someone panics, is magically compelled, or the party attacks first.

{@b Mixing Room.} Formulae and reports explain that Yaren is combining local water, extraplanar residue, and living subjects in an attempt to reproduce the Radiant Well's effects. The party can recover evidence, ingredients, and one useful counteragent here.
{@b Secret Stores.} Hidden chambers contain curated salvage: {@b 400 gp}, useful alchemical supplies, two consumable magic items, and at most one uncommon permanent item appropriate to the party.

entries.name: Upper Level — Control Rooms
entries: {@b Guard Post.} One heavily altered captive has been conditioned to attack anyone who passes without a spoken greeting. Scratched words near the threshold and repeated “hello” marks on the wall reveal the trigger. The party can speak the greeting, calm the captive, disable the door, or fight if necessary.

{@b Fountain Chamber.} Pumps force black contaminant into the river. The machinery has three visible pressure nodes. Characters can shut the system down safely with three successful actions using Arcana, Investigation, thieves' tools, smith's tools, or brute force. On a failed attempt, pressure rises and creates an environmental complication; it never explodes without warning. Once two nodes are disabled, an obvious escalating whine gives everyone one round to retreat before any major rupture.

{@b Yaren's Apartment.} Yaren is a {@creature Mage|XMM} or another arcane NPC appropriate to the party's tier. He wants specimens and research, not martyrdom. He bargains if cornered, uses control magic before lethal magic, and attempts to escape through the teleport pad or exterior route when defeat becomes likely.

{@b Pumping Room.} Three Reedscale prisoners are shackled to the pumping apparatus. They recoil from anyone wearing Yaren's insignia but stop resisting the moment characters begin freeing them. They know Yaren's routines, the teleport sequence, the location of other captives, and the hidden exit.

entries.name: Yaren's Research and Tyren
entries: Yaren is not Tyren's lieutenant. He is an opportunist attempting to imitate phenomena he only partly understands. His notes nevertheless provide another independent clue that the Radiant Well can alter or admit consciousness. This preserves thematic connection without making every villain part of one organization.

entries.name: Resolution
entries: Stopping the pumps and securing the research cleans the river over the following days. Bellweather's trade, sanitation, and access to the eastern ruins improve dramatically. If the Reedscale prisoners are rescued, their settlement becomes a potential regional ally in Chapter 15.

entries.name: Scene 1: The Poisoned River
entries: People along the Storen River report dead fish, skin burns, and magical discoloration in the water.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Sampling the water shows the contamination increases upstream toward Maren Isle.
The party can arrange a boat, use magic, or approach from the far bank.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The contamination is magical runoff, not disease. Protection from poison helps against exposure but does not clean the river.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Every day of delay worsens shortages in Bellweather but does not automatically kill named NPCs.

entries.name: Scene 2: Landing
entries: The island’s lower structures are protected by constructs and altered wildlife.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A submerged intake tunnel offers a covert route. The dock is faster but watched.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: At the dock, use 2 {@creature Animated Armor|XMM} and 2 {@creature Water Weird|XMM|Water Weirds}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Crates are labeled with cemetery catalog numbers, confirming bodies or samples were transferred here.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: A quiet landing prevents laboratory staff from destroying research.

entries.name: Scene 3: Lower Maze
entries: The lower level channels water through unstable magical systems.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Characters can shut three valves to reduce hazards above. Each valve is guarded by environmental effects rather than mandatory combat: scalding steam, arcane surges, or flooding.
DC 14–16 appropriate checks or spells disable each safely.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The systems concentrate energy from old Radiant Well residue carried through subterranean channels.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: For each valve disabled, remove one lair-style hazard from the final laboratory fight.

entries.name: Scene 4: Laboratories
entries: Living captives and magical test subjects are kept here.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Rescue captives before pursuing Yaren if the party wants all survivors safe.
One chamber contains notes comparing living hosts, undead bodies, and dragon physiology.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Chief researcher Yaren is brilliant, contemptuous, and more interested in surviving with his notes than dying for Tyren.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Mage|XMM} for Yaren, 2 {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, and 1 {@creature Invisible Stalker|XMM}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Yaren’s notes say Tyren’s present host is unusually powerful and difficult to control; a bronze dragon is referenced indirectly by size, breath, and metallic physiology.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing Yaren provides a technical explanation of how to interrupt transference. Killing him leaves the notes.

entries.name: Scene 5: Control Rooms
entries: The upper controls govern discharge into the river and contain the best data on Tyren’s experiments.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party must shut down the discharge without causing an arcane rupture. Require three successful DC 15 Arcana, Investigation, or tool checks before two failures; appropriate spells can substitute.
On a failure, each creature in the room takes 2d6 force damage. The system still can be shut down.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Tyren can leave a host when control breaks if another viable host is nearby. The notes recommend isolating potential hosts during any confrontation.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Stopping the discharge restores the river over several days.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 15
entries: The research shows that Tyren is consolidating power beyond Bellweather as well as within it. The city needs allies and safe routes before a final confrontation.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} 400 gp, alchemical supplies, 2 consumables, one uncommon permanent item (default {@b Periapt of Proof against Poison} or equivalent if available; otherwise {@b Cloak of the Manta Ray}).

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Build regional leverage through alliances and selective military action rather than treating every settlement as a dungeon.
Bellweather’s survival now depends on routes and communities outside the city. The party travels beyond the ruins to build alliances before Tyren can isolate Bellweather.
The chapter ends when the party has enough regional allies, safe routes, and intelligence to survive the political crisis that follows Perrin’s betrayal.
{@b Leads onward.} Once the party has enough allies and routes, Perrin Cardon presents a supposedly urgent mission to Zennar Outpost. His betrayal begins the final political crisis.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Secure routes, negotiate alliances, neutralize genuinely hostile warbands, protect communities.
{@b Player agency.} Every settlement/stronghold should offer at least one noncombat path unless its leadership has already chosen immediate violence.
{@b Fail forward.} Diplomatic setbacks change terms and alliances; they do not force extermination.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Current Faction Rule
entries: These communities are not enemy biomes organized by species. Each location is a political or social group with its own leadership, interests, and internal disagreements. Some remain primarily one species because they are kinship communities; others are mixed. The party can negotiate, ally, trade, intimidate, infiltrate, or fight depending on what the faction is actually doing.
{@b Recommended level:} 13–15

entries.name: Table-Ready Use
entries: These wilderness sites are optional alliances, threats, and resources—not a mandatory checklist. Choose the sites that matter to the party's strategy. Currentize each community with current stat blocks and give intelligent factions goals beyond "fight the party."

These wilderness episodes are grouped together here so the adventure can use them as a regional arc rather than interrupting the city chapters at random. Not every group encountered outside Bellweather is an enemy. The party should be able to create alliances, negotiate passage, or exploit rivalries. Use the source lairs and maps while applying current encounter math.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Regional Encounter Notes
entries: Currentize by biome. Favor {@creature Owlbear|XMM}, {@creature Ankheg|XMM}, {@creature Displacer Beast|XMM}, {@creature Ettercap|XMM}, {@creature Troll|XMM}, {@creature Manticore|XMM}, {@creature Bulette|XMM}, {@creature Wyvern|XMM}, {@creature Giant Crocodile|XMM}, {@creature Shambling Mound|XMM}, {@creature Will-o'-Wisp|XMM}, and culturally appropriate humanoid groups. Use reaction and morale; not every encounter is automatically hostile.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/kerren_settlement.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/kerren_settlement.webp}

Kerren is a thri-kreen settlement built among low earthen mounds and connected underground chambers. It is {@b not a treasure dungeon}. The residents are wary because armed outsiders have repeatedly entered their territory looking for relics and valuables.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Kerren sits along a route used by Tyren's couriers. The party may seek intelligence, safe passage, or help identifying troop movements.

{@b First contact.} Communication can happen through magic, gesture, a knowledgeable guide, or patient observation. Good-faith trade and respect for burial sites improve the encounter; theft or desecration turns the settlement hostile.

{@b If combat occurs.} Use current {@creature Thri-kreen|XMM|Thri-kreen} stat blocks appropriate to the party's tier. They use mobility, cover, and withdrawal rather than standing in place until killed.
{@b Reward.} Trusted characters receive regional intelligence, safe passage, supplies, and one uncommon consumable or crafted item. Sacred objects remain with the community.

{@b Bellweather consequence.} A peaceful agreement opens a safer inland route and improves Neighborhoods & Workers reputation. Violence closes that route and gives Tyren's agents an easier propaganda victory.

entries.name: Waylen Camp
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/waylen_camp.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/waylen_camp.webp}

Waylen Camp belongs to a mobile mixed-species community of herders, guides, hunters, and traders. They have no interest in conquering Bellweather and are suspicious of anyone who assumes neutrality means weakness.
{@b Why the party comes here.} The camp has seen troop columns and can identify which factions are moving under Tyren's orders. It also controls access to a reliable route through the grasslands.
{@b Finding the camp.} The party finds an abandoned campsite and fresh tracks pointing toward the current location. No random roll is required if the characters are actually searching the area.

{@b Negotiation.} The camp values useful information, medical aid, fair trade, and proof that Bellweather intends to respect local autonomy. An unprovoked attack destroys this goodwill; defenders hold the perimeter while noncombatants withdraw, and leaders seek a way to end the violence once the immediate threat is contained.
{@b Reward.} Guides, mounts, regional intelligence, and a standing invitation to trade.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} An alliance makes Bellweather less dependent on old merchant families for overland commerce, which quietly threatens Cardon's interests.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/rellan_enclave.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/rellan_enclave.webp}

Rellan is a lizardfolk enclave built around a ruined keep and flooded tunnels. The enclave is a community, not an automatically hostile monster lair. If the party rescued lizardfolk prisoners on Maren Isle, they are recognized as allies before weapons are drawn.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Rellan's elders know regional history that Bellweather's records have lost, including stories connected to the Radiant Well and the poisoned waterways.

{@b Approach.} Characters who arrive openly can request an audience. Characters sneaking into the enclave may be challenged by scouts and giant-lizard handlers, but defenders attempt to identify intruders before escalating to lethal force.

{@b Terrain.} Collapsed masonry and flooded tunnels create {@b Difficult Terrain}. Underwater passages connect several pools; a 10-minute search finds them automatically, while a successful DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check spots them immediately. Use normal 2024 underwater-combat rules.
{@b If combat occurs.} Use current {@b Lizardfolk} and {@b Giant Lizard} stat blocks. Defenders retreat through the water routes when badly outmatched.

{@b Reward.} Allies are welcomed to a feast and receive safe passage, regional lore, and a bronze friendship token recognized by allied communities. Exceptional service can earn one uncommon consumable or crafted weapon.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} Peaceful relations establish a southern ally and challenge the idea that every group outside Bellweather must be conquered or absorbed.

entries.name: Ash Road Warband
entries: The Ash Road Warband is a {@b named hostile faction}, not a stand-in for all orcs. Its members raid settlements, take captives, and serve Tyren because the arrangement gives their leaders weapons, territory, and protection. The force itself can include multiple species.
{@b Why the party comes here.} Refugees report kidnappings and burned caravans. Scouts also connect the warband to Tyren's courier network.

{@b Approach.} The party finds signs of violence before reaching the camp: burned wagons, frightened survivors, and scouts watching the road. A wounded survivor can identify the direction captives were taken; their fate depends on the party's aid rather than a scripted death.

{@b Encounter structure.} Do not run dozens of low-level attackers. Use 6–10 meaningful combatants, a leader, one specialist, and an objective such as opening the captive pen, disabling a signal horn, or preventing a courier from escaping.
{@b Captives.} If the warband threatens prisoners, that creates a rescue clock. Refusing to intervene is a story and reputation consequence, never an alignment punishment.
{@b Treasure.} The war chest contains {@b 2,000 gp} in coin and trade bars, three art objects, two consumable magic items, and one level-appropriate permanent item.
{@b Bellweather consequence.} Rescued captives bring testimony about Tyren's logistics. How Bellweather treats surrendered warband members becomes a visible test of the city's values.

entries.name: Emmer Hold
Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/emmer_hold.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/emmer_hold.webp}

Emmer Hold is a fortified kobold-majority settlement built into old mining works and drainage tunnels. It is {@b not a dungeon full of creatures who exist to be cleared}. Most residents are miners, craftspeople, families, traders, and laborers. A militant faction inside the hold has accepted arms and promises from Tyren's agents in exchange for harassing Bellweather's roads.

entries.name: Why the Party Comes Here
entries: Choose whichever hook follows from play:

items: caravans report disciplined ambushes using Emmer-made traps;
the Council wants safe passage through the nearby road;
a Bellweather merchant claims the entire mine under an old deed, creating a dispute before the party ever arrives;
Emmer dissidents quietly ask for help removing the Tyren-aligned commander.

entries.name: The Situation
entries: {@b Kessa Ember}, a practical kobold engineer, speaks for residents who want neutrality and trade. {@b Daren Voss}, a mixed-species mercenary captain using the {@creature Veteran|XMM} stat block, commands the Tyren-aligned fighters. The militant force consists of {@b Kobold Warriors, Guards, Scouts,} and a small number of specialists; do not deploy mass waves.

The party can resolve Emmer Hold by negotiation, exposing Daren's arrangement with Tyren, defeating his command cell, sabotaging the weapons cache, or convincing residents that Bellweather will recognize their right to remain. A direct assault is possible but immediately damages Regional Standing and turns civilians into evacuees rather than combatants.

items: {@b Outer Works.} Traps, warning bells, and observation points. The challenge is getting close without convincing the whole settlement it is under invasion.
{@b Commons.} Civilian heart of the hold. Violence here has severe political consequences.
{@b Forge Gallery.} Evidence that outside agents supplied military-grade material.
{@b Command Chamber.} Daren and 2–4 elite allies. Use terrain, cover, and a surrender threshold rather than a fight to the death.
{@b Old Treasury.} Most wealth is communal reserve, payroll, and trade stock. The party's actual reward is a curated cache: coin, consumables, and at most one level-appropriate permanent item.

entries.name: Bellweather Consequence
entries: A negotiated settlement can open a new trade route and add kobold engineers to Bellweather reconstruction projects. A conquest secures the road faster but creates refugees, resentment, and a visible test of what “reclamation” means when another community already lives there.

entries.name: Iron Banner Fort
entries: The Iron Banner is a disciplined military faction headquartered in a fortified hill complex. Its core leadership is hobgoblin, but its ranks include several species bound by pay, oath, coercion, family ties, or belief that Tyren offers stability. The fort is a {@b military and civilian settlement}, not an ancestry-coded extermination dungeon.

items: Iron Banner patrols are closing a road Bellweather needs.
Prisoners taken from a caravan are being held for leverage.
A dissident officer offers intelligence in exchange for safe passage.

{@b Doman}, a deceptive spellcaster seeking an artifact in the fort, tries to manipulate the party into doing his work. Use a current {@creature Mage|XMM} stat block and let the party expose or refuse him without losing access to the adventure.

entries.name: Faction Structure
entries: {@b Commander Haren Vell} uses the {@creature Gladiator|XMM} or another appropriate high-tier martial stat block. He is loyal to Tyren because Tyren guarantees supplies and regional authority. {@b Captain Sera Dorn} uses the {@creature Veteran|XMM} stat block and is willing to negotiate if the party can prove Tyren is treating the Iron Banner as disposable. The fort also contains guards, scouts, smiths, healers, families, prisoners, and noncombatant workers.

entries.name: Running the Fort
entries: Treat the fort as five zones rather than thirty rooms of attrition:

items: {@b Outer Patrol Line.} A reconnaissance, stealth, diplomacy, or short skirmish scene. Do not use 25–50 creature waves.
{@b Barracks and Works.} The party can sabotage supplies, free prisoners, gather evidence, or win over soldiers.
{@b Civilian Quarter.} No combat objective requires harming civilians. Their presence is explicit so players understand the faction is a society, not a monster nest.

{@b Temple and Command Hall.} Religious and political leadership can be separated from rank-and-file soldiers. Coercive priests use {@b Cult Fanatic/Priest} style stat blocks; soldiers use current martial NPCs.
{@b Command Vault.} The climactic confrontation centers on Commander Haren, 2–4 elite allies, and an objective such as seizing orders, stopping a signal, or preventing destruction of evidence.

entries.name: Doman's Artifact
entries: The source adventure places an unusually powerful magic cache here. In this adventure, the object Doman wants is a {@b sealed planar vessel} connected to research on the Radiant Well. It is valuable because of what it proves, not because it grants a pile of unrelated powers. If the party keeps it, it functions primarily as a story key until the DM chooses an appropriate level-15 reward.

entries.name: Outcomes
entries: {@b Alliance or armistice:} The Iron Banner withdraws support from Tyren, Regional Standing rises, and Bellweather gains a disciplined neighboring power rather than conquered territory.
{@b Leadership defeat:} The faction fractures; some soldiers surrender or leave, while civilians remain. Bellweather must decide whether to recognize local self-government.
{@b Total assault:} Militarily possible, but costly. Regional Standing falls and Perrin can exploit the bloodshed politically.

entries.name: Treasure
entries: Do not award the source module's enormous coin piles and stacks of +1/+2/+3 gear. The fort's wealth is payroll, communal stores, equipment, and regional trade stock. A successful resolution grants a level-appropriate monetary reward, 2–3 consumables, and at most one permanent rare/very rare item that fits the party and current tier.

entries.name: Chapter Structure
entries: This chapter is a regional alliance arc. The party does not need every community as an ally. Three strong alliances plus a safe route are enough to move forward. Each location should feel like a community with its own interests, not a monster encounter with a settlement attached.

entries.name: Kerren Settlement: The Water Dispute
entries: Kerren is divided over access to a spring after armed outsiders begin taxing travelers.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can expose the outsiders’ connection to Tyren, negotiate a shared water schedule, or drive off the extortionists.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Elder Sella Kerren wants stability and hates being treated as a subordinate of Bellweather.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If fighting occurs, use 1 {@creature Veteran|XMM} and 4 {@creature Thug|XMM|Thugs}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The extortionists carry Storen Gate-era command marks and promises of future authority under Tyren.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Resolve the water dispute fairly and Kerren provides scouts and food.

entries.name: Waylen Camp: The Missing Hunters
entries: Several hunters disappeared after following tracks into old ruins near the camp.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party locates the missing hunters and finds them trapped by a predator rather than enemy soldiers.
Returning them alive matters more than killing the creature.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Waylen’s leader, Jorn Waylen, is suspicious of city promises but respects people who show up when help is needed.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Bulette|XMM}. It attacks from below and retreats if badly injured.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The hunters saw Tyren-aligned couriers avoiding Waylen territory by taking the Ash Road.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Waylen provides guides and a hidden route if helped.

entries.name: Rellan Enclave: The Internal Split
entries: Rellan’s residents are divided between neutrality and alliance with Bellweather.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: A Tyren-aligned agent is paying agitators to sabotage talks. The party can identify the payments, protect a public meeting, and expose the agent.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Speaker Mara Rellan wants proof before taking sides. Young militants want immediate alliance; merchants fear retaliation.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If exposed, the agent uses {@creature Assassin|XMM} and tries to escape rather than fight to the death.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Payment records tie the agent directly to the Ash Road Warband.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Exposing manipulation earns Rellan’s political support and messengers.

entries.name: Ash Road Warband: Break the Command
entries: Unlike the communities, the Ash Road Warband actively raids for Tyren.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can attack the camp, challenge leadership, or turn disaffected members against the commanders.
Targeting food stores or mounts can end the warband’s ability to raid without killing everyone.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: War leader Kesh serves Tyren for promised land and rank. Several lieutenants doubt those promises.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Gladiator|XMM}, 2 {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, and 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts} for the command group.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Orders promise Kesh authority over communities he does not currently control.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Breaking the leadership opens the Ash Road and weakens Tyren’s regional reach.

entries.name: Emmer Hold: The Siege Within
entries: Emmer Hold is technically allied to Bellweather but divided by a commander willing to accept Tyren’s protection.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party arrives during a political standoff. Loyalists hold the inner yard while the commander controls the armory.
The party can negotiate a surrender, expose the commander’s secret orders, or fight for the armory.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Captain Emmer wants the hold to survive and can be persuaded. Commander Darr Vale believes Bellweather is doomed.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If needed, use Darr as a {@creature Knight|XMM} with 4 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Darr’s orders instruct him to delay regional aid until Varen Keep is secure.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Resolving the split gives the party soldiers or supplies for the finale.

entries.name: Iron Banner Fort: The Choice
entries: The fort is a professional military force split between Tyren loyalists and pragmatists.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can present evidence, challenge the command structure, sabotage Tyren’s artifact, or negotiate neutrality.
Avoid treating every soldier as an enemy.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Doman, the fort’s commander, values order and fears chaos more than Tyren.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: If open combat occurs, use small squads of {@creature Knight|XMM|Knights} and {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}; do not run the entire fort on one initiative.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Doman possesses an artifact used to receive Tyren’s orders. Destroying or exposing it proves the command relationship.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Alliance provides elite troops; neutrality prevents reinforcements reaching Tyren; hostility creates one extra complication in Chapter 17.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 16
entries: Once the party has enough allies and routes, Perrin Cardon presents a supposedly urgent mission to Zennar Outpost. His betrayal begins the final political crisis.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Ash Road war chest 2,000 gp + 2 consumables + one rare item. Iron Banner/Emmer rewards are primarily alliance, access, supplies, and one rare/very rare item total across the regional arc. Avoid stacking permanent rewards from every settlement.

data.name: Chapter 16: The Zennar Outpost
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 15–16

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Survive Perrin’s betrayal, preserve proof, and return to a Bellweather where official institutions have been turned against the party.
Perrin gives the party an apparently legitimate high-priority mission to Zennar Outpost. The orders are designed to put them where they can be killed or discredited.
The chapter ends with the party outside normal legal protection, relying on allies they earned during the campaign while they gather enough proof to expose Perrin.
{@b Leads onward.} Evidence from Zennar and earlier chapters confirms that Tyren’s central power remains at Varen Keep and that his current host must be separated from the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Identify the hidden order, escape or turn the outpost, preserve proof.
{@b Player agency.} Expose the message early, negotiate with the outpost, fake compliance, escape, or fight.
{@b Fail forward.} The betrayal cannot hinge on one Investigation roll; the evidence surfaces through orders, testimony, or intercepted communication.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

entries.name: Table-Ready Purpose
entries: Run this as a political betrayal and survival chapter. The documents Cardon sends with the party are evidence against him. Use {@b Veterans}, {@b Knights}, {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies}, and {@b Mages} rather than a mass garrison encounter. Escape, negotiation, and exposing Cardon are more important than defeating the whole outpost.

This mission should occur after Cardon has enough influence to plausibly send the party away and arrange their deaths. The return to Bellweather becomes a political chapter: the party must survive, prove the betrayal, and decide what kind of authority the Council should have afterward.

entries.name: Cardon's Public Reassurance
entries: While the characters are away, Perrin prepares the public story before they can tell their own. Notices and statements describe rumors of Council corruption as irresponsible speculation and insist that Bellweather's administration remains stable. His preferred line is familiar:
{@b "Bellweather's recovery remains secure. There is no cause for alarm."}

This is the phrase at its most political. Perrin is not merely calming frightened citizens; he is using reassurance to define dissent as panic and to make legitimate warnings sound reckless. Characters who preserved older Council notices or the Marren Library circular can explicitly point out the repetition when they return. Doing so should matter socially even if it does not automatically prove his crimes.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Treat this as political danger as much as combat. Use {@creature Veteran|XMM}, {@creature Knight|XMM}, {@creature Mage|XMM}, {@creature Spy|XMM}, {@creature Assassin|XMM}, and other current humanoid stat blocks according to role. Preserve the diplomatic trap and evidence that exposes Cardon.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Approaching the Outpost
entries: Zennar is a disciplined stone-and-timber stockade on a defensible rise. A cavalry patrol meets unknown travelers and requests that they enter under escort. The patrol is suspicious, professional, and interested in the party's connection to Bellweather.
Characters can:

items: enter openly as envoys;
inspect the packet before arrival and attempt to reseal it;
approach covertly to observe the post first;
contact a trader, prisoner, or low-ranking soldier outside the walls;
refuse entry and negotiate at the gate.

entries.name: Discovering the Trap
entries: Opening Cardon's packet reveals the betrayal directly. Without opening it, characters can still notice warning signs: the commandant becomes unusually interested in where they are sleeping, guards are assigned as watchers rather than escorts, and staff quietly remove civilians from their corridor. A successful Wisdom (Insight) or Intelligence (Investigation) check gives earlier warning, but the clue is never locked behind one roll.

entries.name: Inside Zennar
entries: If welcomed as envoys, the party receives quarters and a controlled tour. The outpost contains soldiers with different loyalties; not everyone knows about the assassination order. Characters who build rapport can discover that the commandant received instructions from Bellweather that same day.

If the party is detained, they are treated as valuable political prisoners. Their equipment is secured separately. Use imprisonment as a {@b fail-forward sequence} with opportunities for bribery, outside help, forged orders, negotiation, or escape. Do not end the adventure through forced enslavement or an unwinnable mass battle.

entries.name: The Assassination Attempt
entries: If the party remains overnight without exposing the plot, three {@b Veterans} and one {@creature Mage|XMM}, supported by four {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards}, attempt a quiet arrest-and-kill operation. They gain only the advantages they have actually earned through stealth and positioning. Roll attacks and saving throws normally; sleeping characters use the normal 2024 rules.
The attackers withdraw if the operation becomes loud or clearly fails. Most of the garrison believes the disturbance is an external attack, creating confusion the characters can exploit.

entries.name: Getting Out
entries: The party can escape through the main gate, over the wall, through a service route, disguised among a departing patrol, or with help from someone they befriended. Reinforcements arrive as {@b pressure}, not as hundreds of creatures placed on the battle map.

entries.name: Proof Against Cardon
entries: The commandant's copy of the instruction bears Cardon's seal and phrasing. Captured assassins know they were following a written order delivered from Bellweather. Either source is enough to point the party back toward Cardon; obtaining both makes the political case much stronger.

entries.name: Return to Bellweather
entries: Cardon has used the party's absence to shape the story. Public notices describe the envoys as unstable, compromised, or missing and repeat Perrin's familiar reassurance. The party must decide whether to return openly with evidence, enter quietly and gather allies, or force a Council hearing.

entries.name: Scene 1: Perrin’s Mission
entries: Perrin presents sealed Council orders directing the party to Zennar Outpost to secure evidence of enemy coordination.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The orders look legitimate and use real Council seals. Perrin stresses secrecy and speed.
If the party independently verifies them, a clerk confirms the seal but notes the authorization number belongs to a different minor requisition. This is the first chance to suspect a trap.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin is calm and concerned, not theatrical. He wants the party gone before questions spread.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The paperwork is technically forged through misuse of legitimate records, foreshadowing how Perrin weaponizes institutions.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Discovering the forgery early lets the party approach Zennar cautiously but does not cancel the chapter.

entries.name: Scene 2: Approach to Zennar
entries: The outpost looks undermanned because the ambushers are concealed.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Scouts can spot prepared firing positions, fresh horse tracks, and supplies for more troops than are visible.
A friendly-looking sentry attempts to bring the party into the central yard.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The sentry carries a list of the party’s names and descriptions.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: If the party refuses the yard, the ambush begins from less favorable positions for the attackers.

entries.name: Scene 3: Discovering the Trap
entries: Inside the command office are duplicate orders accusing the party of treason and authorizing lethal force.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party can seize the papers, question a clerk, or search the records room.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Clerk Elin Voss is frightened and did not know the party would be killed. She admits the documents arrived through Perrin’s office.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The records include a prepared public statement blaming the party for unauthorized violence at Zennar.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Elin is a powerful witness if protected.

entries.name: Scene 4: Assassination Attempt
entries: The hidden strike team attacks once the party has enough evidence to be dangerous.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The attackers focus on isolating and finishing individual characters rather than defending territory.
An escape route through the supply tunnel allows a tactical withdrawal.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Strike leader Varek Holt has been promised immunity and money by Perrin. He knows the political purpose of the mission but not Tyren’s plans.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use 1 {@creature Assassin|XMM}, 2 {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, and 4 {@creature Scout|XMM|Scouts}.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Varek carries a payment order routed through a Cardon-controlled intermediary.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Capturing Varek gives direct testimony; killing him leaves documentary proof.

entries.name: Scene 5: Return as Criminals
entries: Perrin moves before the party can return.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Public notices accuse the characters of exceeding authority, killing lawful agents, stealing records, or conspiring with hostile factions depending on what happened at Zennar.
The party’s previous allies determine whether they have safe houses, sympathetic guards, messengers, and public credibility.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Brakkus shelters civilians connected to the party and refuses to hand over guests without lawful cause, but he does not attack the city government on the party’s behalf.
Wern and Bishop Brann demand evidence before taking a public position.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The Zennar orders, Elin, Varek, and financial records are four independent ways to prove the betrayal. The party needs two credible forms of evidence to break Perrin’s position.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: This chapter turns earlier faction relationships into concrete resources.

entries.name: Scene 6: Exposing Perrin
entries: Run the exposure as a political confrontation, not a courtroom simulation unless the players want one.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The party presents evidence to Councilors, the public, allied factions, or all three. Perrin attacks credibility and procedure rather than confessing.

If evidence is strong, Perrin loses institutional protection and attempts to flee or bargain. If evidence is weaker, regional allies and public witnesses can force an investigation that removes his immediate authority.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Perrin believes he used Bellweather’s institutions to preserve order and his own power. He does not reveal himself as a servant of Tyren because he is not one.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Perrin’s betrayal is human political ambition, separate from Tyren’s supernatural domination.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Once Perrin is neutralized, the party can move openly against Varen Keep.

entries.name: Transition to Chapter 17
entries: Evidence from Zennar and earlier chapters confirms that Tyren’s central power remains at Varen Keep and that his current host must be separated from the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} No conventional dungeon hoard. Evidence is the primary reward. Outpost can provide 1,000 gp-equivalent diplomatic restitution if peacefully resolved.

data.name: Chapter 17: Varen Keep and the Radiant Well
entries: {@b Recommended level:} 16

entries.name: Maps
entries: {@link Player Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/player/varen_keep.webp}
{@link DM Keyed Map|https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sefjoe/no-cause-for-alarm-5etools/main/img/dm/varen_keep.webp}

entries.name: Chapter Overview
entries: {@b Session purpose.} Break Tyren’s control, free or defeat Soren without reducing the finale to a static dragon fight, and decide the fate of the Radiant Well.
With Perrin exposed or politically broken, the party moves against Varen Keep, the center of Tyren’s remaining power.

Victory is not just killing an enemy. The campaign ends with the characters deciding who controls the Well, what political order replaces Perrin’s influence, and what kind of city Bellweather becomes.

entries.name: Running the Chapter
entries: {@b Primary objectives.} Reach Tyren, break control systems/allies, survive the host confrontation, decide the Well’s fate.
{@b Player agency.} Assault, infiltration, exploit internal factions, use recovered lore, or create a political/military coalition.
{@b Fail forward.} Knowledge needed to challenge Tyren has been seeded across Savin Keep, Marren Library, Maren Isle, and Cardon’s records.

{@b Rest and pressure.} Safe long rests are available back at Ledger House. Inside the active adventure site, resting gives opposing factions time to reposition unless the characters secure a defensible refuge.

### ##### Treasure Override By the finale, strong items are appropriate, but avoid a sudden old-school cache. Award at most {@b one major permanent item per character} across the entire castle, with the Pool itself treated as a story object rather than portable treasure.

entries.name: Encounter Guidance
entries: Use the {@creature Adult Bronze Dragon|XMM} as Soren's base stat block. Tyren is represented narratively as the possessing intelligence and mechanically with a limited fiery-aura/possession overlay described in this chapter. For a second phase, use a {@creature Efreeti|XMM} stat block reskinned as Tyren temporarily manifesting in flame if the group needs a level-16 climax. Avoid the Ancient Bronze Dragon stat block for a four-character level-16 party unless the group is unusually optimized.

{@b Keyed-area encounters.} When a scene and a keyed location describe the same encounter, use the roster and objective in the scene. Creatures listed only in the keyed reference apply when the characters explore that location outside the scene sequence.

entries.name: Location and Background Details
entries: Varen Keep is the adventure climax. Do {@b not} clear it room by room. Use the source map for geography, then run the keep as a sequence of infiltration choices and 3–5 set pieces that feed the three-phase finale above.

entries.name: Area Description
entries: The outer compound has been cleared for lines of sight. Guards, servants, coerced workers, and Tyren's advisors occupy the surrounding buildings. At the center stands the decaying tower. The bailey has been converted into a thorn maze whose black flowers glow faintly when the Radiant Well surges.

{@b Thorn Maze.} A creature forcing through a hedge must make a {@b DC 15 Dexterity saving throw}, taking {@b 3d6 piercing plus 3d6 poison damage} and becoming {@b Poisoned until the end of its next turn} on a failure. Cutting a person-sized gap requires 30 damage from suitable weapons or tools. Creative magic can bypass the maze normally.

{@b Teleporters.} Four marked spaces connect unpredictably. When a creature activates one, roll 1d4 to determine the destination among the four pads. A character who studies two activations can make a DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) check to identify the pattern and choose a destination thereafter.

entries.name: Keyed Areas
entries: Only the areas below need full treatment. Other numbered rooms on the map are empty, storage, ordinary quarters, or connective spaces unless circumstances during play make them relevant.

{@b 2. Watchpost.} A {@creature Veteran|XMM} officer and 2 {@creature Guard|XMM|Guards} monitor the outer compound. The alarm can be disabled, forged, or redirected. Capturing the watchpost gives advantage on the party's next infiltration check.
{@b 5. Officer's Quarters.} Contains a fragment of the Radiant Well map, {@b 200 gp}, and one useful consumable. The fragment confirms details learned in Marren Library.

{@b 8. Guard Barracks.} Use 2–4 {@b Ogres} or an equivalent tier-appropriate mixed guard detail. A rigged sand bucket is a visible nuisance trap: DC 13 Dexterity save or 1d4 bludgeoning damage and {@b Blinded until the end of the creature's next turn}.

{@b 10. Warband Barracks.} Eight off-duty members of Tyren's mixed garrison rest here. If alerted, they use bunks as cover and attempt to hold the corridor until reinforcements arrive. Their effects include {@b 20 gp}, a duty roster, and the day's watch password.

{@b 11. Alen's Quarters.} {@b Alen Hyam} is a {@creature Mage|XMM} advisor who has intentionally been fed false information by Tyren. He prefers conversation, surrender, or escape to combat. His notes contain one false conclusion and two useful observations about the Well. Use the current Mage stat block exactly as printed.
{@b 12. Main Gate.} The party can use the password, sabotage the mechanism, climb elsewhere, or force the gate. A frontal breach attracts a manageable reinforcement wave rather than an army.

{@b 20. Servants' Hall and Kitchen.} Coerced workers of mixed species know the day's password and the rhythm of the guard rotations. Freeing them removes one reinforcement from Phase 1 and improves Neighborhoods & Workers reputation.

{@b 22. Records Room.} Ten minutes of focused review reveals the pattern of Tyren's growing political and military influence. A successful DC 15 Intelligence (Investigation) check reveals it immediately and also uncovers a report documenting Cardon's dealings. This evidence matters if Cardon's political fate remains unresolved.

{@b 23. Medusa Chamber.} A captive {@creature Medusa|XMM} has been used as a living security measure. She is furious at Tyren, not automatically at the party. Characters who offer freedom can turn her into a temporary ally or source of information. If combat begins, use the current Medusa stat block exactly as printed.

{@b 27. Smithy.} An armorer ({@creature Veteran|XMM}) and three {@creature Bugbear Warrior|XMM|Bugbears} maintain mundane equipment. They initially assume the party belongs to Tyren's forces if the characters act confidently. The room contains quality mundane gear, {@b 20 gp}, and tools useful for sabotaging a control node.

{@b 31. False Tyren Chamber.} An impostor ({@creature Gladiator|XMM} or {@creature Veteran|XMM}) and two {@creature Spy|XMM|Spies} maintain a decoy command room. If exposed, the impostor may surrender and explain the deception. The room holds {@b 1,000 gp} in portable valuables and a counterfeit seal.

{@b 36. Blackstone Shrine.} A small Bane shrine serves members of Tyren's coalition. Use a {@creature Cult Fanatic|XMM}, two {@b Acolytes}, and 4–6 mixed worshippers or soldiers only if the scene adds something. The blessing offered here is coercive magic: DC 15 Wisdom save or the target is {@b Cursed}, suffering disadvantage on saves against fear and charm effects created by Bane's servants until {@spell Remove Curse|XPHB} or similar magic ends it. It never changes alignment, class, or personality.

{@b 40. Jeren's Study.} {@b Jeren} is a rival advisor who believes Tyren may eventually discard him. He can be bribed, frightened, recruited, or exposed. If he betrays the party, he uses his current spellcasting and escapes if possible rather than fighting to the death.

{@b 44. Tyren's Audience Chamber.} Tyren may speak through Soren here before the final battle. He offers status and command to test what the characters value. Accepting does not automatically remove player agency; any supernatural control uses the finale's possession procedure and requires the relevant game effect to succeed.

entries.name: Set-Piece Sequence
entries: Choose three to five of the following before Phase 2:

items: {@b Silent Entry:} bypass the gate and disable the watchpost.
{@b Free the Workers:} secure passwords and remove reinforcements.
{@b Turn an Advisor:} convince Alen, Jeren, or the medusa to help.
{@b Destroy a Control Node:} sabotage a Well-linked device in the maze or tower.
{@b Expose the Decoy:} defeat or flip the false Tyren group.
{@b Secure the Records:} recover Cardon/Tyren evidence and Well lore.

entries: Each success removes one complication or grants one concrete advantage in the finale. Failure advances Tyren's alert level but never blocks access to the climax.

entries.name: Phase 2: Soren, the Host
entries: Use an {@creature Adult Bronze Dragon|XMM} as Soren's base chassis. Soren is a victim of possession. Tyren's control gives the encounter environmental effects linked to any surviving control nodes. Characters can damage Soren, but the adventure repeatedly signals that breaking the control is the better solution.

entries.name: Phase 3: Transference
entries: When Tyren is expelled, the entity attempts to move through the Radiant Well's conduit. The party can stop it by combining recovered lore with actions at the Well: sealing runes, breaking a conduit, using a recovered relic, or willingly taking a dangerous temporary burden. This phase is solved by objectives and choices, not by reducing another hit-point total to zero.

entries.name: The Fate of the Radiant Well
entries: After Tyren is defeated, the characters choose what happens to the Well:

items: {@b Destroy it:} removes the immediate danger but loses a source of knowledge and power.
{@b Seal it:} preserves the site while making access difficult and politically contested.
{@b Study it:} creates opportunity and risk; Bellweather must decide who controls the research.
{@b Steward it:} place the Well under a new institution, alliance, or set of rules shaped by the party.

entries: The final epilogue should show the consequences in Bellweather rather than declare one choice objectively correct.

entries.name: Finale Overview
entries: The finale is not a room-by-room extermination. It is an assault on a command center followed by a multi-stage effort to free Soren, stop Tyren’s transference, and decide the fate of the Radiant Well. Let earlier alliances remove or soften obstacles.

entries.name: Scene 1: Approach to Varen Keep
entries: Choose the approach based on alliances and intelligence earned earlier.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Possible routes include the main gate with allied troops, a river approach revealed by Waylen scouts, a service passage from old records, or infiltration using captured signals.
For every major regional ally, remove one outer complication: patrols, artillery, blocked route, or reinforcement wave.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: The keyed DM map marks major set-piece areas rather than requiring every room to be cleared.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The party’s campaign choices materially affect how difficult the assault feels.

entries.name: Scene 2: Breaking the Command Network
entries: Before confronting Soren, the party can disable three control nodes in the keep.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: The signal chamber coordinates troops. The ritual chamber reinforces possession. The reserve host chamber contains captives selected as possible vessels.
Each node disabled grants one finale benefit: no reinforcement wave, Soren loses one defensive advantage, or Tyren has fewer transference targets.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Use encounters already listed in the chapter’s keyed areas, favoring {@creature Veteran|XMM|Veterans}, {@creature Mage|XMM|Mages}, and small elite groups rather than mass combat.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Captives confirm that Soren is a bronze dragon being controlled, not a willing tyrant.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Skipping nodes is allowed but makes the final phases harder.

entries.name: Scene 3: Soren, Host of Tyren
entries: Soren confronts the party under Tyren’s control.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Use the official {@creature Adult Bronze Dragon|XMM} as Soren’s base stat block. Tyren forces him to fight intelligently but cruelly, targeting isolation and control rather than dragon instincts.
The party can damage Soren, disrupt the possession focus, invoke evidence or memories that strengthen Soren’s resistance, or use the laboratory methods learned on Maren Isle.

At the end of each round after the ritual node is disabled, one character adjacent to a control focus can use an action to attempt DC 17 Arcana, Religion, or Persuasion. Three total successes weaken Tyren enough to begin separation.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Soren cannot freely communicate while possessed, but brief hesitation or broken phrases show he is still present.

entries.name: Encounter
entries: Adult Bronze Dragon plus environmental hazards from the chapter. Do not add unrelated monsters unless the party skipped outer objectives.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Maren Isle research explains why potential new hosts must be kept away when separation begins.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: Reducing Soren to 0 hit points is not required. If that happens before separation, Tyren immediately attempts transference.

entries.name: Scene 4: Transference
entries: When Tyren loses control of Soren, the intelligence tries to enter another viable host.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Any uncontrolled captive, major NPC, or character in the Radiant Well chamber can become a target. If the reserve host chamber was cleared, Tyren has fewer options.
The party can isolate targets, destroy conduits, use protective magic, or redirect Tyren into the Well itself.
Run this as a 4-success group challenge before 3 complications. Arcana, Religion, Constitution saves, protective spells, and creative plans can contribute.

entries.name: Clues and Discoveries
entries: Tyren is a possessing intelligence; destroying one host never guaranteed victory. This is the payoff to clues from Savin Keep, Marren Library, Valen Cemetery, and Maren Isle.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: On a complication, Tyren briefly controls a target for one turn, triggers a Well surge, or damages the chamber. Do not permanently take a PC away on one failed roll.

entries.name: Scene 5: The Radiant Well
entries: Once Tyren is contained, the party must decide what happens to the Well.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Options include sealing it, placing it under shared civic custody, destroying its access structures, studying it under strict safeguards, or another solution the players devise.
No institution has an automatic right to control it. Present arguments from allies and surviving officials, then let the players decide.

entries.name: NPC Behavior
entries: Brakkus argues only that no single person should be able to quietly control something capable of taking away another person’s will. Wern worries about defense. Bishop Brann worries about moral danger. Scholars argue that ignorance is also dangerous.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The final decision should echo the campaign’s questions about power, ownership, legitimacy, and who bears the risk of rebuilding.

entries.name: Scene 6: Bellweather Afterward
entries: End with concrete consequences rather than a generic victory celebration.

entries.name: What Happens
entries: Describe streets the party reopened, people they saved, factions they changed, and institutions they challenged.
Resolve Perrin’s remaining assets and influence according to Chapter 16.
Name which communities remain allied, which precedents govern property, and who oversees the Radiant Well.

entries.name: Consequences
entries: The phrase “There is no cause for alarm” can appear one final time only if it now means responsible confidence rather than denial. The healthier Bellweather listens to warnings instead of suppressing them.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: {@b Treasure and rewards.} Across the keep, no more than one major permanent item per PC total, chosen to fit gaps in existing equipment. The Well itself is a story object, never portable loot.

entries.name: Four Reputation Tracks
entries: Start each at 0; range -2 to +2.

items: {@b Council}
{@b Neighborhoods & Workers}
{@b Merchants & Investors}
{@b Independent Factions}

entries: At +2, grant one meaningful favor per chapter when reasonable. At -2, create one active complication per chapter. Reputation never overrides obvious consequences or roleplay.

entries.name: Perrin Cardon Escalation

items: {@b Useful heir (levels 3–5).} Smart, polished, one vote among several.
{@b Successful claimant (levels 6–8).} Wealth/property return; he funds private security and civic projects.
{@b Power broker (levels 9–11).} Controls information, allies, contracts, and increasingly the public narrative.
{@b Institutional rival (levels 12–15).} Can delay hearings, shape notices, pressure merchants, and frame opponents as destabilizing.
{@b Betrayer (level 15–16).} Uses Zennar mission to remove the party while preserving legal distance.

entries: Do not make Perrin openly villainous ahead of the evidence. Give him legitimate successes and arguments so his eventual abuse of power feels earned rather than pre-announced.

entries.name: Tyren Reveal Ladder

items: Separate hostile groups share signals and supplies.
The “Boss” coordinates groups that normally compete.
Historical records show the same impossible coordination during Bellweather's fall.
Savin Keep names Tyren and radiant water.
Marren Library establishes host transfer/possession.
Maren Isle independently confirms the Well's consciousness effects.
Regional factions explain how Tyren mixes money, threats, alliance, and supernatural domination.
Varen Keep reveals Soren as the current host.

entries: Never require one roll for any step. If a clue is essential, the party receives it from the correct location/person.

a new business/worker/refugee group;
changing prices or rents;
a property dispute;
a new patrol/gate/route;
a public notice;
a benefit ordinary residents can name;
a cost ordinary residents can name;

entries.name: Brakkus Boundary
entries: Brakkus Ledgerhelm is a roughly 48-year-old {@b half-orc, level 16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Torm} and retired adventurer. He runs Ledger House because that is the life he chose after adventuring. He is formidable enough to make serious violence under his roof a poor decision, but he is not the party's regular quest-giver, field companion, political leader, or solution to Bellweather's problems. Use his full stat block only when violence reaches him or people under his protection.

entries.name: Brakkus Ledgerhelm
entries: Brakkus is a roughly forty-eight-year-old {@b half-orc, level 16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Torm}, retired from adventuring and now the proprietor of Ledger House. His mother Elena was a captive librarian in the Ironfang Clan; his father was the warlord Korgak. After Elena's death, Brakkus rejected his father's bloodline, took the surname Ledgerhelm in her honor, and later trained under High Justiciar Vance Halford. Vance gave him the +3 longsword Brakkus named {@item The Appendix|NCFA}.

Brakkus is the stable home-base NPC. He does not need to accompany missions or dominate Council politics. His retirement is a choice, not a loss of ability. Use him to make Bellweather feel inhabited: he remembers names, knows who has been displaced, notices when new money arrives, and can tell when official success looks different from ordinary people's lives.

Do not make Brakkus secretly central to Perrin, Tyren, or the player characters' personal arcs. He offers shelter, introductions, rumors, occasional perspective, and protection of Ledger House. His combat statistics matter mainly if danger reaches his home or civilians under his protection.

entries.name: Cardon and the Inequality Theme
entries: Cardon's ambition should remain clear. His inherited claim, resentment, Council position, private guards, recovered family wealth, and manipulation of public reclamation for private advantage are central to the adventure's theme. He is not wrong because he is wealthy; he is dangerous because he treats public risk and public institutions as tools for restoring what he believes his family deserves.

entries.name: Tyren
entries: Tyren is a different kind of domination: direct supernatural control. This creates useful contrast with Cardon's legal and economic power. The campaign can explore coercion at both institutional and supernatural scales without making every antagonist part of one conspiracy.

data.name: Appendix D: Maps
entries: Player-facing maps appear in the chapters where they are used. Keyed versions for the Dungeon Master are collected in the DM Map Index at the end of the adventure.
When a map label differs from the adventure text, the names used in the chapter are correct for play.

data.name: Appendix E: Rumors, Downtime, and Returning to Ledger House

entries.name: Phase Rumors
entries: Roll or choose one rumor when the party returns to Ledger House. Rumors are leads, not all confirmed facts.

items: “Half the buildings they marked safe last week already have three people claiming them.”
“Somebody at Kellan's Well is paying patrols from different crews with the same stamped chits.”
“Blackstone's people are taking food as ‘donations’ now.”
“Perrin Cardon actually got a roof repaired for six families. Didn't even put his name on it. Much.”
“The old keep out in the harbor lights up some nights with nobody living there.”
“Council says the storm damage is localized. The carpenter sleeping by the stove says otherwise.”
“Property near the reopened road doubled in price before the road was officially announced.”
“Cardon guards are better paid than the Watch.”
“Someone is buying old maps of the library and not asking what they cost.”
“Savin Keep's records say the old enemy armies marched like one army.”
“The people living in the Mansion District are worried the heirs are coming back with papers and guards.”
“Every merchant swears recovery is good for everyone. Every renter swears the merchant means someone else.”
“The Square is open again, and somehow I can afford less there than when it was occupied.”
“Gate permits are already worth more than some houses.”
“Something is taking people near Valen Cemetery after dark.”
“The river's poison gets worse around Maren Isle.”
“The Council says coordinated attacks are localized. Brakkus bought extra lamp oil.”
“Perrin has started speaking for the Council even when nobody asked him to.”
“Kerren's people remember every agreement. Bellweather's people remember every profit.”
“The Iron Banner is asking whether Tyren can actually protect anyone anymore.”
“Perrin's notices call criticism ‘panic.’ That's a new word for disagreement.”
“Somebody is quietly collecting copies of everything the party brought back from Marren Library.”
“The Zennar road has more riders on it than usual.”
“People keep asking what happens when the ruins are reclaimed. Nobody agrees on who ‘we’ means.”

entries.name: Downtime Menu
entries: Each character gets one downtime beat between major expeditions unless the fiction is urgent.

items: {@b Gather Information:} one rumor plus a named source.
{@b Build Relationship:} deepen one NPC/faction connection; after meaningful roleplay, gain advantage on one future social check with that contact or shift attitude.
{@b Research:} gain one extra context clue tied to an already-discovered lead.
{@b Work Reclamation:} gain Neighborhoods & Workers goodwill; once per tier, convert this into +1 reputation after a meaningful project.
{@b Craft/Commission:} use current 2024 crafting and local availability.
{@b Train/Carouse:} use current 2024 downtime guidance; success should create a contact, proficiency progress, or useful rumor rather than filler.

entries.name: Ledger House Return Procedure
entries: Every return should take 5–15 minutes at the table unless players linger.

items: Describe one physical change in Bellweather.
Put one familiar person in the common room.
Give one consequence of the party's last choice.
Offer two rumors/opportunities, only one of which needs to be the “next chapter.”
Let Brakkus react briefly if the players seek him out; he does not summon them for plot delivery.

data.name: Appendix F: Session Prep Template
entries: Use this one-page structure when turning a chapter into a session.

entries.name: Session Goal
entries: Write one sentence describing what can materially change tonight.

items: {@b Arrival/choice:} present the problem and at least two approaches.
{@b Pressure:} encounter, investigation, negotiation, hazard, or combat that complicates the plan.
{@b Decision:} a consequence-bearing choice or objective encounter.

entries.name: Essential Information
entries: List every clue the players must receive for the adventure to continue. Do not attach these to single pass/fail checks.

entries.name: Opposition
entries: For each active faction, write {@b goal / current position / what makes them retreat or negotiate}.

entries.name: Rest Clock
entries: Write one thing the opposition does if the characters take a long rest in hostile territory.

entries.name: Rewards
entries: Choose treasure from the chapter override plus one non-item reward: reputation, access, property use, an ally, a civic favor, or information.

entries.name: Return to Ledger House
entries: Prepare:

items: one visible Bellweather change;
one Brakkus observation or dry remark;
one consequence of the party's choice;
two rumors or opportunities pointing forward.

trait.name: Aura of Protection
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him gain a +4 bonus to saving throws.

trait.name: Aura of Courage
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him can't be {@condition frightened}.

trait.name: Aura of Devotion
entries: While Brakkus is conscious, he and friendly creatures within 10 feet of him can't be {@condition charmed}.

trait.name: Purity of Spirit
entries: Brakkus is continuously under the effects of {@spell Protection from Evil and Good|XPHB}.

trait.name: Relentless Endurance (1/Long Rest)
entries: When Brakkus is reduced to 0 hit points but not killed outright, he drops to 1 hit point instead.

trait.name: Lay on Hands (80 HP/Long Rest)
entries: Brakkus has a pool of 80 hit points of healing. As an action, he can touch a creature and restore any number of hit points remaining in the pool. He can instead spend 5 points to cure one disease or neutralize one poison affecting the target.

trait.name: Fire Walker
entries: Brakkus can stand on and move across molten rock as if it were solid ground.

trait.name: Paladin Spellcasting
entries: Brakkus's spellcasting ability is Charisma (spell save DC 17, +9 to hit with spell attacks).
At will: {@spell Sacred Flame|XPHB}, {@spell Word of Radiance|XPHB}
1/Long Rest: {@spell Shield|XPHB} (from Magic Initiate)

Prepared Paladin Spells (use spell slots): {@spell Lesser Restoration|XPHB}, {@spell Zone of Truth|XPHB}, {@spell Beacon of Hope|XPHB}, {@spell Dispel Magic|XPHB}, {@spell Freedom of Movement|XPHB}, {@spell Guardian of Faith|XPHB}
Spell Slots: 1st level (4), 2nd level (3), 3rd level (3), 4th level (2)

action.name: Multiattack
entries: Brakkus makes two attacks with {@item The Appendix|NCFA}.

action.name: The Appendix
entries: {@atk mw} {@hit 12} to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. {@h}11 ({@damage 1d8 + 7}) slashing damage plus 2 ({@damage 1d4}) radiant damage.

action.name: Divine Smite
entries: When Brakkus hits a creature with The Appendix, he can expend a spell slot to deal additional radiant damage: 2d8 with a 1st-level slot, 3d8 with a 2nd-level slot, 4d8 with a 3rd-level slot, or 5d8 with a 4th-level slot. The damage increases by 1d8 against a Fiend or Undead, subject to the normal Divine Smite maximum.

action.name: Sacred Flame
entries: One creature Brakkus can see within 60 feet must succeed on a DC 17 Dexterity saving throw or take 13 ({@damage 3d8}) radiant damage. The target gains no benefit from Half Cover or Three-Quarters Cover for this save.

action.name: Word of Radiance
entries: Each creature of Brakkus's choice within 5 feet of him must succeed on a DC 17 Constitution saving throw or take 10 ({@damage 3d6}) radiant damage.

action.name: Sacred Weapon (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus imbues The Appendix with positive energy for 1 minute. He adds his Charisma modifier (+4) to attack rolls made with the weapon, raising its attack bonus to +16, and the weapon emits bright light in a 20-foot radius and dim light for another 20 feet.

action.name: Turn the Unholy (Channel Divinity; 1/Short or Long Rest)
entries: As an action, Brakkus presents his holy symbol. Each Fiend or Undead within 30 feet that can see or hear him must succeed on a DC 17 Wisdom saving throw or be Turned for 1 minute or until it takes damage.

reaction.name: Shield (1/Long Rest)
entries: When Brakkus is hit by an attack roll or targeted by {@spell Magic Missile|XPHB}, he casts {@spell Shield|XPHB}. Until the start of his next turn, his AC becomes 29, including against the triggering attack, and he takes no damage from Magic Missile.
Brakkus is a roughly forty-eight-year-old half-orc, retired adventurer and mercenary, and level 16 Oath of Devotion paladin of Torm. He owns Ledger House in Bellweather and maintains it as a refuge.
Brakkus is a home-base NPC, not a companion character. His default priorities are protect civilians, stabilize downed allies, contain the threat, then defeat the aggressor.
Challenge Rating. The listed CR is provided for encounter-building purposes; Brakkus is a 16th-level paladin.

item.name: The Appendix
entries: You gain a +3 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic longsword.
On a hit, the weapon deals an extra {@damage 1d4} radiant damage.
The Appendix was given to Brakkus Ledgerhelm by High Justiciar Vance Halford and named in honor of Elena's love of books.
The item does not require attunement.
